global_indicators.1-1-1-definition: This indicator corresponds to the sum of people who are: at risk of poverty after social transfers,  severely materially and socially deprived, or living in households with very low work intensity.  Individuals are counted only once, even if they are affected by more than one of these occurrences.  People are considered at risk of poverty if their income is below 60% of the national median  equivalent disposable income.
global_indicators.1-1-1-intention: Poverty and social exclusion limit people's opportunities to reach their full potential by affecting  health and reducing educational outcomes. Without effective social protection, the risk of poverty  is passed between generations, creating inequality and hindering sustainable economic growth.  The long-term objective for this indicator is a value of 0.
global_indicators.1-1-1-methodology: Based on the Europe-wide harmonised annual survey on income and living conditions (EU-SILC).  From 2020 onwards, data is not strictly comparable with previous years due to methodological  revisions and integration into the microcensus.
global_indicators.1-1-1-title: People at risk of poverty or social exclusion
global_indicators.1-10-definition:
The indicator is part of the EU Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) indicator set. It is used to monitor progress towards SDG 1 on ending poverty in all its forms everywhere and SDG 10 on reducing inequality within and among countries which are embedded in the European Commission’s Priority under 'Supporting people, strenghtening our societes and our social model'. This indicator corresponds to the sum of people who are: at risk of poverty after social transfers, severely materially and socially deprived, or living in households with very low work intensity. Individuals are counted only once, even if they are affected by more than one of these occurrences.
•	People are considered at risk of poverty after social transfers if their equivalent disposable income is not higher than the poverty risk threshold, which is set at 60% of the national median equivalent disposable income.
•	Severe material and social deprivation rate is the share of the population experiencing a forced lack of at least 7 out of 13 deprivation items (6 relate to the individual, and 7 to the household)
global_indicators.1-10-intention: Poverty and social exclusion are harmful to individual lives and limit people's opportunities to reach their full potential by affecting their health and well-being and reducing educational outcomes. This, in turn, reduces opportunities for a successful life and further increases the risk of poverty. Without an effective system of education, healthcare, social protection, tax relief, and employment, the risk of poverty is passed from one generation to the next. This causes the persistence of poverty and thereby creates even more inequality, which can lead to long-term loss of economic productivity of entire groups of society and hinder inclusive and sustainable economic growth.
global_indicators.1-10-long_term_objective: The long-term objective for this indicator is a value of 0
global_indicators.1-10-methodology: The data used for this indicator is based on the Europe-wide harmonised annual survey on income and living conditions (EU-SILC). In the 2020 survey year, EU-SILC underwent extensive methodological revisions and was integrated into the microcensus in response to increasing demands for up-to-date data and the provision of more detailed regional results. As a result of this realignment, the data from 2020 onwards is not comparable with that of previous years. Since 2021, Regulation (EU) 2019/1700 provides for requirements relating to geographical coverage, detailed sample characteristics, including sub-sampling, in accordance with Annex III, common data collection periods, common standards for editing and imputation, weighting, estimation and variance estimation.
global_indicators.1-10-title: Persons at risk of poverty or social exclusion
global_indicators.1-2-1-definition: The income quintile share ratio (S80/S20) is the ratio of total equivalised disposable income received by the top 20% of the population to that received by the bottom 20%. A higher value indicates greater income inequality. Data are drawn from the EU Survey on Income and Living Conditions (EU-SILC).
global_indicators.1-2-1-intention: Income inequality undermines social cohesion and limits life opportunities for those at the lower end of the income distribution. Reducing inequality is a prerequisite for sustainable and inclusive growth. Progress means a decreasing S80/S20 ratio over time.
global_indicators.1-2-1-methodology: Data are collected through EU-SILC. Equivalised disposable income is the total household income after tax and other deductions, divided by the equivalised household size. The survey is conducted annually in all participating countries.
global_indicators.1-2-1-title: Persons at risk of monetary poverty after social transfers
global_indicators.1-2-2-title: Proportion of men, women and children of all ages living in poverty in all its dimensions according to national definitions
global_indicators.1-20-definition: The EU-SILC collection is a key instrument for providing the information required by the European Semester([1]) and the European Pillar of Social Rights. It is also the main source of data for microsimulation purposes and for producing flash estimates of income distribution and poverty rates. The indicator of persons at risk of poverty or social exclusion (AROPE) remains crucial for monitoring European social policies, especially for monitoring the EU 2030 target on poverty and social exclusion. The European Union Statistics on Income and Living Conditions (EU-SILC) collects timely and comparable multidimensional microdata on income, poverty, social exclusion and living conditions. Statistical concepts and definitions for EU-SILC are specified in EU regulation 2019/1700, EU regulation 2019/2181, and EU regulation 2019/2242. The basic Regulation and its implementing and delegated acts provided for multiple changes to the EU-SILC data collection starting from 2021. Countries must follow Annex II to EU regulation  2019/2242, where the list of variables is set out, including their modalities, flags, unit and reference period.
global_indicators.1-20-long_term_objective: The long-term objective for this indicator is a value of 0
global_indicators.1-20-methodology: The target population is private households and all persons composing these households having their usual residence in the national territory. A private household means a person living alone or a group of persons who live together, providing for themselves the essentials of living. The concept of accuracy refers to the precision of estimates computed from a sample rather than from the entire population. Accuracy depends on sample size, sampling design effects and the structure of the population being studied. In addition, sampling errors and non-sampling errors need to be considered. Sampling error means the variability that occurs at random due to using a sample rather than a census, and non-sampling errors are errors that occur in all phases of the data collection and production process. From 2021 EU regulation 2019/1700 lays down the requirements relating to geographical coverage, detailed sample characteristics, including subsampling, in accordance with Annex III to that Regulation, sampling characteristics, common data gathering periods, common standards for editing and imputation, weighting, estimation and variance estimation.
global_indicators.1-20-title: Persons at risk of monetary poverty after social transfers - EU SILC and ECHP surveys
global_indicators.1-3-1-definition: This indicator measures the proportion of the population covered by at least one social protection benefit, including benefits related to old age, disability, sickness, unemployment, family and housing. It is expressed as a percentage of the total population. Data are based on EU-SILC.
global_indicators.1-3-1-intention: Effective social protection systems prevent poverty and reduce the impact of economic shocks on individuals and families. Broad coverage ensures that those in need receive timely support. Progress means extending effective coverage to all segments of the population.
global_indicators.1-3-1-methodology: Data are collected from EU-SILC, which gathers information on social transfers received by households. The indicator covers both contributory (insurance-based) and non-contributory (means-tested) benefits across all categories of social protection.
global_indicators.1-3-1-title: Severe material and social deprivation rate by age group and sex
global_indicators.1-31-definition: The ‘Income and Living Conditions’ (EU-SILC) domain covers the following topics: persons at risk of poverty or social exclusion, income inequality, income distribution and monetary poverty, living conditions and material deprivation. It also covers EU-SILC ad hoc modules, which are organised into collections of indicators on specific topics. The EU-SILC collection is a key instrument for providing the information required by the European Semester ([1]) and the European Pillar of Social Rights. It is also the main source of data for microsimulation purposes and for producing flash estimates of income distribution and poverty rates. In 2024, in addition to annual data, EU-SILC collected the three-yearly module on children health, access to healthcare and children specific deprivation, and the six-yearly module on access to services. The information collected in EU-SILC pertains to the following types of statistical units: private households and persons living in those households. Annex II to EU regulation 2019/2242 defines the specific statistical units for each variable, while Annex IV to the same Regulation specifies the content of the quality reports on the organisation of a sample survey in the income and living conditions domain, pursuant to EU regulation 2019/1700 of the European Parliament and of the Council.
global_indicators.1-31-long_term_objective: The long-term objective for this indicator is a value of 0
global_indicators.1-31-methodology: The target population is private households and all persons composing these households having their usual residence in the national territory. A private household means a person living alone or a group of persons who live together, providing for themselves the essentials of living. The reference period is the survey year. For all countries, the reference period for income variables in EU-SILC is the previous calendar year. The concept of accuracy refers to the precision of estimates computed from a sample rather than from the entire population. Accuracy depends on sample size, sampling design effects and the structure of the population being studied. In addition, sampling errors and non-sampling errors need to be considered. Sampling error means the variability that occurs at random due to using a sample rather than a census, and non-sampling errors are errors that occur in all phases of the data collection and production process. From 2021 EU regulation 2019/1700 lays down the requirements relating to geographical coverage, detailed sample characteristics, including subsampling, in accordance with Annex III to that Regulation, sampling characteristics, common data gathering periods, common standards for editing and imputation, weighting, estimation and variance estimation.
global_indicators.1-31-title: Severe material and social deprivation rate by age group and sex
global_indicators.1-4-1-definition: The housing cost overburden rate is the proportion of the population living in households where total housing costs (net of housing allowances) represent more than 40% of total disposable household income. It is expressed as a percentage. Data are based on the EU Statistics on Income and Living Conditions (EU-SILC).
global_indicators.1-4-1-intention: Excessive housing costs reduce disposable income available for other necessities and increase the risk of poverty and social exclusion. Monitoring this indicator helps identify households under financial strain from housing costs. Progress means a reduction in the proportion of people overburdened by housing costs.
global_indicators.1-4-1-methodology: Data are collected through EU-SILC. Housing costs include rent, mortgage repayments, utilities and maintenance. Housing allowances are deducted from both costs and income before calculating the 40% threshold. The survey is conducted annually.
global_indicators.1-4-1-title: Persons living in households with very low work intensity, by age group
global_indicators.1-4-2-definition: The severe housing deprivation rate is the proportion of the population living in an overcrowded dwelling that also lacks at least one of the following: a bath or shower, an indoor flushing toilet, or has a leaking roof or damp walls. It is expressed as a percentage. Data are based on EU-SILC.
global_indicators.1-4-2-intention: Adequate housing is a fundamental human need and a key determinant of health and well-being. Severe housing deprivation directly impacts physical and mental health, educational attainment and social participation. Progress means a sustained reduction in the severe housing deprivation rate.
global_indicators.1-4-2-methodology: Data are collected through EU-SILC. Overcrowding is assessed relative to household size and composition. Housing quality deprivation covers structural problems (leaking roof, damp walls) and the absence of basic facilities (bath or shower, indoor toilet).
global_indicators.1-4-2-title: In work at risk of poverty rate
global_indicators.1-40-definition: Poverty and social exclusion harm individual lives and limit the opportunities for people to achieve their full potential by affecting their health and well-being and lowering educational outcomes. This, in turn, reduces opportunities to lead a successful life and further increases the risk of poverty. Without effective education, health, social, tax benefit and employment systems, the risk of poverty is passed on from one generation to the next. This causes poverty to persist and hence creates more inequality, which can lead to long-term loss of economic productivity from whole groups of society and hamper inclusive and sustainable economic growth.
global_indicators.1-40-intention: People in the age of 0 to 64 years living in households where the adults worked a working time equal or less than 20 % of their total combined work-time potential during the previous year. As adults count people in the age of 18 to 64 years. Students aged 18 to 24 years; people who are retired according to their self-defined current economic status or who receive any pension (except survivor’s pension); and people in the age bracket 60 to 64 who are inactive and living in a household where the main income is pensions, are not taken into account. The indicator is part of the multidimensional poverty index.
global_indicators.1-40-long_term_objective: The long-term objective for this indicator is a value of 0
global_indicators.1-40-methodology: The reference period is the survey year. For all countries, the reference period for income variables in EU-SILC is the previous calendar year. The indicator is included as a secondary indicator in the Social Scoreboard for the European Pillar of Social Rights and the EPSR Action Plan, and is part of the multidimensional poverty index. It can be considered as part of the global SDG indicator 1.2.2 "Proportion of men, women and children of all ages living in poverty in all its dimensions according to national definitions" From 2021 Regulation (EU) 2019/1700 foresees the requirements relating to geographical coverage, detailed sample characteristics, including subsampling, in accordance with Annex III, common data gathering periods, common standards for editing and imputation, weighting, estimation and variance estimation.
global_indicators.1-40-title: Persons living in households with very low work intensity, by age group
global_indicators.1-41-definition: The indicator is part of the EU Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) indicator set where it is used to monitor progress towards SDG 1 on ending poverty in all its forms everywhere, which is embedded in the European Commission’s Priorities under 'An Economy that works for people'. The indicator is included as a secondary indicator in the Social Scoreboard for the European Pillar of Social Rights and EPSR Action Plan. The share of persons who are employed and have an equivalised disposable income below the risk-of-poverty threshold, which is set at 60 % of the national median equivalised disposable income (after social transfers). For the purpose of this indicator, an individual is considered as being employed if he/she was employed for more than half of the reference year. The indicator is based on the EU-SILC (statistics on income, social inclusion and living conditions).
global_indicators.1-41-intention: Employment is often claimed to be the best protection against poverty, so one of the objectives of the EU is to create more and better jobs. It is therefore important to measure the share of working-poor, people living below the poverty line although they are working. Poverty and social exclusion harm individual lives and limit the opportunities for people to achieve their full potential by affecting their health and well-being and lowering educational outcomes. This, in turn, reduces opportunities to lead a successful life and further increases the risk of poverty. Without effective education, health, social, tax benefit and employment systems, the risk of poverty is passed on from one generation to the next. This causes poverty to persist and hence creates more inequality, which can lead to long-term loss of economic productivity from whole groups of society and hamper inclusive and sustainable economic growth.
global_indicators.1-41-long_term_objective: The long-term objective for this indicator is a value of 0
global_indicators.1-41-methodology: The indicator is produced according to the high-level quality standards of European Statistics. From 2005 onwards, EU-SILC is based on a common framework defined by harmonised lists of primary and secondary variables, common concepts, a recommended design, common requirements (such as imputation procedures, weighting, sampling errors calculation) and classifications aiming at maximising comparability of the information produced. From 2021 Regulation (EU) 2019/1700 foresees the requirements relating to geographical coverage, detailed sample characteristics, including subsampling, in accordance with Annex III, common data gathering periods, common standards for editing and imputation, weighting, estimation and variance estimation
global_indicators.1-5-1-definition: This indicator tracks deaths and economic losses attributed to disaster events, including natural hazards such as floods, storms, droughts and extreme temperatures. It is used to assess population resilience to climate-related and other disaster events. Data are compiled from national civil protection authorities and international databases.
global_indicators.1-5-1-intention: Building resilience to disasters is key to protecting lives, livelihoods and development gains. Countries with effective disaster risk reduction strategies and social safety nets suffer fewer disaster-related deaths and smaller economic losses. Progress means a reduction in disaster-related mortality and losses.
global_indicators.1-5-1-methodology: Data are collected from national civil protection and emergency management authorities, complemented by international databases such as EM-DAT. The indicator covers disaster events that require emergency response and result in human or significant economic losses.
global_indicators.1-5-1-title: Housing cost overburden rate by poverty status
global_indicators.1-5-2-title: Direct economic loss attributed to disasters in relation to global gross domestic product (GDP)
global_indicators.1-5-3-title: Number of countries that adopt and implement national disaster risk reduction strategies in line with the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030
global_indicators.1-5-4-title: Proportion of local governments that adopt and implement local disaster risk reduction strategies in line with national disaster risk reduction strategies
global_indicators.1-50-definition: The indicator is part of the EU Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) indicator set where it is used to monitor progress towards SDG 1 on ending poverty in all its forms everywhere, which is embedded in the European Commission’s Priorities under 'Supporting people, Strenghtening our societes and our social model'. The indicator is included as a secondary indicator in the Social Scoreboard for the European Pillar of Social Rights and the EPSR Action Plan, and is part of the multidimensional poverty index. It can be considered as part of the global SDG indicator 1.2.2 "Proportion of men, women and children of all ages living in poverty in all its dimensions according to national definitions".
global_indicators.1-50-intention: Poverty and social exclusion harm individual lives and limit the opportunities for people to achieve their full potential by affecting their health and well-being and lowering educational outcomes. This, in turn, reduces opportunities to lead a successful life and further increases the risk of poverty. Without effective education, health, social, tax benefit and employment systems, the risk of poverty is passed on from one generation to the next. This causes poverty to persist and hence creates more inequality, which can lead to long-term loss of economic productivity from whole groups of society and hamper inclusive and sustainable economic growth.
global_indicators.1-50-long_term_objective: The long-term objective for this indicator is a value of 0
global_indicators.1-50-methodology: The indicator measures the share of population living in households that spend 40 % or more of the household disposable income on housing ('net' of housing allowances). Housing costs include rental or mortgage interest payments but also the cost of utilities such as water, electricity, gas or heating. From 2021 Regulation (EU) 2019/1700 foresees the requirements relating to geographical coverage, detailed sample characteristics, including subsampling, in accordance with Annex III, common data gathering periods, common standards for editing and imputation, weighting, estimation and variance estimation.
global_indicators.1-50-title: Housing cost overburden rate by poverty status
global_indicators.1-a-1-title: Total official development assistance grants from all donors that focus on poverty reduction as a share of the recipient country’s gross national income
global_indicators.1-a-2-title: Proportion of total government spending on essential services (education, health and social protection)
global_indicators.1-a-3-title: Sum of total grants and non-debt-creating inflows directly allocated to poverty reduction programmes as a proportion of GDP
global_indicators.10-1-1-definition: Ratio of total equivalised disposable income of the richest 20% to that of the poorest 20% of the population. Measures income inequality. Higher values indicate greater inequality. Data from EU-SILC.
global_indicators.10-1-1-intention: Income inequality limits social mobility and cohesion. Progress means a declining S80/S20 ratio reflecting a narrowing gap between richest and poorest.
global_indicators.10-1-1-methodology: Data collected through EU-SILC using equivalised disposable income. Divides total income of top quintile by that of bottom quintile. Published annually by Eurostat.
global_indicators.10-2-1-definition: Difference between the median income of people below the poverty threshold and the threshold itself, expressed as a percentage of the threshold. Measures the depth of poverty. Data from EU-SILC.
global_indicators.10-2-1-intention: The poverty gap shows how far below the poverty line the poor are. Progress means a reduction in the gap, reflecting improved incomes among those at risk of poverty.
global_indicators.10-2-1-methodology: Data from EU-SILC. Poverty threshold set at 60% of national median equivalised disposable income. Gap expressed as percentage of threshold. Published annually by Eurostat.
global_indicators.10-20-title: Disparities in household income per capita
global_indicators.10-3-1-definition: Share of total equivalised disposable income received by the bottom 40% of the income distribution, expressed as a percentage. Higher share indicates more equal distribution. Data from EU-SILC.
global_indicators.10-3-1-intention: Monitoring the bottom 40% income share directly measures inclusive growth. Progress means an increasing income share for the poorest 40%.
global_indicators.10-3-1-methodology: Data collected through EU-SILC. Equivalised disposable income ranked and cumulative share of bottom 40% calculated. Published annually by Eurostat.
global_indicators.10-3-1-title: Income share of the bottom 40% of the population
global_indicators.10-4-1-definition: Number of persons applying for international protection per million inhabitants. Reflects migration pressures and protection needs. Data compiled by Eurostat from national asylum authorities.
global_indicators.10-4-1-intention: Ensuring safe and orderly migration and protection is a dimension of reducing inequalities. Monitoring asylum applications helps assess migration dynamics and policy responses.
global_indicators.10-4-1-methodology: Compiled from national asylum authorities under EU asylum statistics regulations. Covers persons lodging applications for international protection. Published monthly and annually by Eurostat.
global_indicators.10-5-1-definition: Gini coefficient measuring inequality in the distribution of equivalised disposable income. Ranges from 0 (perfect equality) to 100 (maximum inequality). Data collected through EU-SILC.
global_indicators.10-5-1-intention: Income inequality limits opportunities and social mobility. Progress means a declining Gini coefficient reflecting more equal income distribution.
global_indicators.10-5-1-methodology: Data collected through EU-SILC. Gini coefficient calculated from the full income distribution using equivalised disposable income. Published annually by Eurostat.
global_indicators.10-5-1-title: Gini coefficient of equivalised disposable income
global_indicators.10-50-title: Income share of the bottom 40 % of the population
global_indicators.10-6-1-title: Proportion of members and voting rights of developing countries in international organizations
global_indicators.10-7-1-title: Recruitment cost borne by employee as a proportion of monthly income earned in country of destination
global_indicators.10-7-2-title: Number of countries with migration policies that facilitate orderly, safe, regular and responsible migration and mobility of people
global_indicators.10-7-3-title: Number of people who died or disappeared in the process of migration towards an international destination
global_indicators.10-7-4-title: Proportion of the population who are refugees, by country of origin
global_indicators.10-a-1-title: Proportion of tariff lines applied to imports from least developed countries and developing countries with zero-tariff
global_indicators.10-b-1-title: Total resource flows for development, by recipient and donor countries and type of flow (e.g. official development assistance, foreign direct investment and other flows)
global_indicators.10-c-1-title: Remittance costs as a proportion of the amount remitted
global_indicators.11-1-1-definition: Proportion of the total population living in cities (urban areas), expressed as a percentage. Monitors urbanisation trends. Data compiled by Eurostat using the Degree of Urbanisation classification.
global_indicators.11-1-1-intention: Cities drive growth but face challenges of congestion and inequality. Monitoring urbanisation helps plan for sustainable cities. Progress requires urban growth accompanied by adequate infrastructure and services.
global_indicators.11-1-1-methodology: Compiled using the Degree of Urbanisation (DEGURBA) methodology. Cities defined as areas with at least 50,000 inhabitants and density above 1,500/km². Published periodically by Eurostat.
global_indicators.11-2-1-definition: Proportion of the population living in overcrowded dwellings (too few rooms relative to household size), expressed as a percentage. Reflects inadequate housing, especially in urban areas. Data collected through EU-SILC.
global_indicators.11-2-1-intention: Overcrowding affects health and quality of life. Progress means a sustained reduction in the proportion living in overcrowded dwellings.
global_indicators.11-2-1-methodology: Data collected through EU-SILC using a standardised room-to-person ratio definition. Published annually by Eurostat.
global_indicators.11-20-title: Population living in households suffering from noise
global_indicators.11-3-1-definition: Recycling rate of municipal waste in urban areas as a percentage of total waste generated. Reflects progress in sustainable urban waste management. Data compiled by Eurostat.
global_indicators.11-3-1-intention: Sustainable cities need efficient waste management. Increasing recycling in urban areas supports the circular economy. Progress means an increasing urban recycling rate.
global_indicators.11-3-1-methodology: Compiled from national waste statistics under the Waste Statistics Regulation. Includes material recycling and composting. Published annually.
global_indicators.11-3-2-title: Proportion of cities with a direct participation structure of civil society in urban planning and management that operate regularly and democratically
global_indicators.11-4-1-definition: Population-weighted mean annual exposure to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) in micrograms per cubic metre. PM2.5 causes respiratory and cardiovascular disease. Data compiled by the EEA from air quality monitoring networks.
global_indicators.11-4-1-intention: Air pollution is the leading environmental cause of premature death in Europe. Progress means a sustained reduction in population-weighted PM2.5 exposure.
global_indicators.11-4-1-methodology: Compiled by the EEA from national monitoring networks under the Ambient Air Quality Directive. Population-weighted using modelled concentrations and population density. Published annually.
global_indicators.11-4-1-title: Population exposure to air pollution by PM2.5
global_indicators.11-5-1-definition: Share of rail in total inland passenger transport, expressed as a percentage of passenger-kilometres. Reflects use of sustainable alternatives to private cars. Data compiled by Eurostat from national transport statistics.
global_indicators.11-5-1-intention: Rail transport is more energy-efficient and less polluting than private cars. Progress means an increasing share of rail in total passenger transport.
global_indicators.11-5-1-methodology: Data compiled by Eurostat from national transport statistics. Measured in passenger-kilometres. Rail compared to total inland passenger transport. Published annually.
global_indicators.11-5-1-title: Share of rail transport in passenger transport
global_indicators.11-5-2-title: Direct economic loss attributed to disasters in relation to global gross domestic product (GDP)
global_indicators.11-52-title: Premature deaths due to exposure to fine particulate matter (PM2.5)
global_indicators.11-6-1-title: Proportion of municipal solid waste collected and managed in controlled facilities out of total municipal waste generated, by cities
global_indicators.11-6-2-title: Annual mean levels of fine particulate matter (e.g. PM2.5 and PM10) in cities (population weighted)
global_indicators.11-7-1-title: Average share of the built-up area of cities that is open space for public use for all, by sex, age and persons with disabilities
global_indicators.11-7-2-title: Proportion of persons victim of physical or sexual harassment, by sex, age, disability status and place of occurrence, in the previous 12 months
global_indicators.11-a-1-title: Number of countries that have national urban policies or regional development plans that (a) respond to population dynamics; (b) ensure balanced territorial development; and (c) increase local fiscal space
global_indicators.11-b-1-title: Number of countries that adopt and implement national disaster risk reduction strategies in line with the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030
global_indicators.11-b-2-title: Proportion of local governments that adopt and implement local disaster risk reduction strategies in line with national disaster risk reduction strategies
global_indicators.11-c-1-title: Proportion of financial support to the least developed countries that is allocated to the construction and retrofitting of sustainable, resilient and resource-efficient buildings utilizing local materials
global_indicators.12-1-1-definition: GDP divided by domestic material consumption (DMC), expressed in euros per kilogram. Higher resource productivity means more economic output per unit of material. Data compiled by Eurostat from material flow accounts.
global_indicators.12-1-1-intention: Improving resource productivity decouples growth from material use and reduces environmental pressures. Progress means a sustained increase in resource productivity.
global_indicators.12-1-1-methodology: Calculated using GDP and domestic material consumption from material flow accounts (MFA). Both indicators compiled under the EU material flow accounts framework. Published annually.
global_indicators.12-2-1-definition: Total municipal waste generated per inhabitant per year in kilograms. Includes household waste and similar sources. Data compiled by Eurostat from national waste statistics.
global_indicators.12-2-1-intention: Reducing waste generation is the first priority in the waste hierarchy. Progress means a declining trend in municipal waste per capita.
global_indicators.12-2-1-methodology: Compiled by Eurostat from national waste statistics under the Waste Statistics Regulation. Data are published annually.
global_indicators.12-2-2-title: Domestic material consumption, domestic material consumption per capita, and domestic material consumption per GDP
global_indicators.12-3-1-definition: Proportion of municipal waste that is recycled, expressed as a percentage of total waste generated. Covers material recycling and composting. Data compiled by Eurostat from national waste statistics.
global_indicators.12-3-1-intention: Increasing recycling reduces landfilling and resource extraction. Progress means an increasing share of municipal waste being recycled.
global_indicators.12-3-1-methodology: Compiled by Eurostat from national waste statistics under the Waste Statistics Regulation. Includes material recycling and composting. Published annually.
global_indicators.12-4-1-definition: Total GHG emissions per unit of GDP in kilograms of CO₂ equivalent per GDP unit (constant prices). Tracks decoupling of economic growth from emissions. Compiled by Eurostat.
global_indicators.12-4-1-intention: Reducing GHG intensity is essential for sustainable production. Progress means a sustained decline in emissions per unit of GDP.
global_indicators.12-4-1-methodology: Compiled from national GHG inventories and national accounts under ESA 2010. Published annually by Eurostat.
global_indicators.12-4-1-title: Greenhouse gas emissions intensity of production
global_indicators.12-4-2-title: (a) Hazardous waste generated per capita; and (b) proportion of hazardous waste treated, by type of treatment
global_indicators.12-5-1-definition: Share of material recovered and reused as a proportion of overall material use. Indicates progress towards a circular economy. Compiled by Eurostat from waste and material flow statistics.
global_indicators.12-5-1-intention: Increasing circular material use reduces extraction, waste and environmental pressures. Progress means an increasing circular material use rate.
global_indicators.12-5-1-methodology: Calculated as recycled waste used as raw material inputs divided by overall material use. Compiled by Eurostat annually from waste statistics and material flow accounts.
global_indicators.12-6-1-title: Number of companies publishing sustainability reports
global_indicators.12-61-title: Gross value added in environmental goods and services sector
global_indicators.12-7-1-title: Number of countries implementing sustainable public procurement policies and action plans
global_indicators.12-8-1-title: Extent to which (i) global citizenship education and (ii) education for sustainable development are mainstreamed in (a) national education policies; (b) curricula; (c) teacher education; and (d) student assessment
global_indicators.12-a-1-title: Installed renewable energy-generating capacity in developing countries (in watts per capita)
global_indicators.12-b-1-title: Implementation of standard accounting tools to monitor the economic and environmental aspects of tourism sustainability
global_indicators.12-c-1-title: Amount of fossil-fuel subsidies per unit of GDP (production and consumption)
global_indicators.13-1-1-definition: Total national GHG emissions (CO₂, CH₄, N₂O and F-gases) indexed to a base year, expressed as a percentage of base year emissions. Tracks overall progress in reducing emissions. Data reported under UNFCCC.
global_indicators.13-1-1-intention: Reducing total GHG emissions is the central objective of climate policy. Progress means a sustained declining trend in the emissions index.
global_indicators.13-1-1-methodology: Data reported by national authorities under UNFCCC using IPCC methodology. Covers all sectors. Published annually by Eurostat.
global_indicators.13-1-2-title: Number of countries that adopt and implement national disaster risk reduction strategies in line with the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030
global_indicators.13-1-3-title: Proportion of local governments that adopt and implement local disaster risk reduction strategies in line with national disaster risk reduction strategies
global_indicators.13-2-1-definition: Total GHG emissions from the energy sector in million tonnes of CO₂ equivalent. Covers combustion in power plants, refineries and other energy industries. Reported under UNFCCC and compiled by Eurostat.
global_indicators.13-2-1-intention: The energy sector is the largest source of GHG emissions. Decarbonising energy production is essential for meeting climate targets. Progress means a sustained reduction in energy sector emissions.
global_indicators.13-2-1-methodology: Reported by national authorities under UNFCCC using IPCC methodology. Covers CRF sector 1A (fuel combustion) and 1B (fugitive emissions). Published annually.
global_indicators.13-2-2-title: Total greenhouse gas emissions per year
global_indicators.13-21-title: Net greenhouse gas emissions of the LULUCF sector
global_indicators.13-3-1-definition: Economic losses from weather and climate-related extreme events as a percentage of GDP. Includes floods, storms, droughts and heatwaves. Data compiled from civil protection databases and reinsurance sources.
global_indicators.13-3-1-intention: Climate change increases extreme weather events and economic losses. Progress means limiting economic losses from climate-related events through adaptation and mitigation.
global_indicators.13-3-1-methodology: Data compiled from national reports, CATDAT database and reinsurance sources. Covers insured and uninsured losses from weather-related events. Published periodically by Eurostat and the EEA.
global_indicators.13-3-2-title: Number of countries that have communicated the strengthening of institutional, systemic and individual capacity-building to implement adaptation, mitigation and technology transfer, and development actions
global_indicators.13-31-title: Average CO2 emissions per km from new passenger cars
global_indicators.13-4-1-definition: GHG emissions from energy use divided by gross inland energy consumption, expressed in grams of CO₂ equivalent per kilogram of oil equivalent. Reflects the carbon content of the energy mix. Compiled by Eurostat from national energy balances and GHG inventories.
global_indicators.13-4-1-intention: Decarbonising the energy system is central to climate action. Progress means a sustained reduction in the GHG emission intensity of energy.
global_indicators.13-4-1-methodology: Compiled by Eurostat from national energy balances and GHG inventories. Covers combustion and fugitive emissions. Published annually.
global_indicators.13-4-1-title: Greenhouse gas emission intensity of energy consumption
global_indicators.13-50-title: Contribution to the international 100bn USD commitment on climate related expenditure
global_indicators.13-a-1-title: Amounts provided and mobilized in United States dollars per year in relation to the continued existing collective mobilization goal of the $100 billion commitment through to 2025
global_indicators.13-b-1-title: Number of least developed countries and small island developing States with nationally determined contributions, long-term strategies, national adaptation plans and adaptation communications, as reported to the secretariat of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
global_indicators.14-1-1-definition: Proportion of territorial seas and exclusive economic zones designated as marine protected areas (MPAs), as a percentage. Data compiled by the EEA from national designations.
global_indicators.14-1-1-intention: MPAs protect marine biodiversity and ecosystems. Progress means an increasing proportion of seas under effective marine protection.
global_indicators.14-1-1-methodology: Data compiled by the EEA from national designations under Natura 2000 and international conventions. Published annually.
global_indicators.14-2-1-definition: Proportion of assessed commercial fish stocks in EU waters fished at or below maximum sustainable yield (MSY), expressed as a percentage of all assessed stocks. Data compiled by ICES.
global_indicators.14-2-1-intention: Overfishing depletes stocks and damages marine ecosystems. Progress means an increasing proportion of stocks fished within sustainable limits.
global_indicators.14-2-1-methodology: Based on stock assessments conducted by ICES. Sustainability assessed relative to MSY. Covers commercially important stocks in EU and adjacent waters. Published annually.
global_indicators.14-21-title: Estimated trends in fish stock biomass
global_indicators.14-3-1-definition: Concentration of chlorophyll-a in coastal and transitional waters as a proxy for eutrophication. Higher concentrations indicate algal growth from nutrient pollution. Data compiled from marine monitoring programmes.
global_indicators.14-3-1-intention: Eutrophication degrades marine ecosystems. Reducing nutrient inputs is essential for healthy seas. Progress means stable or declining chlorophyll-a concentrations.
global_indicators.14-3-1-methodology: Data compiled from national marine monitoring and satellite remote sensing. Reported under the Marine Strategy Framework Directive and compiled by the EEA.
global_indicators.14-3-1-title: Chlorophyll-a concentration in coastal and transitional waters
global_indicators.14-4-1-definition: Proportion of the coastline experiencing erosion as a percentage of total assessed coastline. Compiled by the EEA using satellite monitoring and the EUROSION database.
global_indicators.14-4-1-intention: Coastal erosion is accelerating due to sea level rise and human pressures. Progress means limiting the proportion of coastline experiencing erosion.
global_indicators.14-4-1-methodology: Data compiled by the EEA using Copernicus Land Monitoring and historical shoreline position comparisons. Published periodically.
global_indicators.14-40-title: Bathing sites with excellent water quality
global_indicators.14-5-1-title: Coverage of protected areas in relation to marine areas
global_indicators.14-6-1-title: Degree of implementation of international instruments aiming to combat illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing
global_indicators.14-7-1-title: Sustainable fisheries as a proportion of GDP in small island developing States, least developed countries and all countries
global_indicators.14-a-1-title: Proportion of total research budget allocated to research in the field of marine technology
global_indicators.14-b-1-title: Degree of application of a legal/regulatory/ policy/institutional framework which recognizes and protects access rights for small-scale fisheries
global_indicators.14-c-1-title: Number of countries making progress in ratifying, accepting and implementing through legal, policy and institutional frameworks, ocean-related instruments that implement international law, as reflected in the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, for the conservation and sustainable use of the oceans and their resources
global_indicators.15-1-1-definition: Forest area as a percentage of total land area, covering forests and other wooded land. Monitors changes due to land use change, afforestation and deforestation. Data compiled by Eurostat from national forestry statistics.
global_indicators.15-1-1-intention: Forests are essential for biodiversity, carbon sequestration and livelihoods. Progress means maintaining or increasing the share of land covered by forests.
global_indicators.15-1-1-methodology: Data compiled from national forestry statistics under the Joint Forest Sector Questionnaire (JFSQ). Forest area defined per FAO criteria. Published periodically by Eurostat.
global_indicators.15-1-1-title: Forest area as share of total land area
global_indicators.15-1-2-title: Proportion of important sites for terrestrial and freshwater biodiversity that are covered by protected areas, by ecosystem type
global_indicators.15-2-1-definition: Proportion of terrestrial and freshwater areas designated as protected, as a percentage of total land area. Includes Natura 2000 and nationally designated areas. Data compiled by Eurostat and the EEA.
global_indicators.15-2-1-intention: Protected areas are a cornerstone of biodiversity conservation. Progress means an increasing proportion of land and freshwater under effective protection.
global_indicators.15-2-1-methodology: Data compiled from national designations reported to the EEA. Natura 2000 forms the backbone of the EU network. Covers both terrestrial and freshwater habitats. Published annually.
global_indicators.15-3-1-definition: Index tracking changes in common bird populations across Europe using 1990 as base year (= 100). Birds are sensitive indicators of ecosystem health. Data compiled from national breeding bird surveys.
global_indicators.15-3-1-intention: Declining bird populations signal habitat degradation. Progress means halting and reversing the decline in common bird populations.
global_indicators.15-3-1-methodology: Data compiled from national breeding bird surveys via the Pan-European Common Bird Monitoring Scheme (PECBMS). Index aggregates trends for representative species. Published annually.
global_indicators.15-4-1-definition: Rate of soil loss caused by water erosion in tonnes per hectare per year. Soil erosion reduces agricultural productivity and degrades ecosystems. Estimated using the RUSLE2015 model by the JRC.
global_indicators.15-4-1-intention: Soil is a non-renewable resource. Reducing soil erosion is essential for sustainable land management and food security. Progress means a reduction in estimated soil loss rates.
global_indicators.15-4-1-methodology: Estimated using the Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (RUSLE2015) model applied to European conditions. Published by the Joint Research Centre (JRC) and Eurostat.
global_indicators.15-4-2-title: Mountain Green Cover Index and proportion of degraded mountain land
global_indicators.15-5-1-definition: Number of invasive alien species of EU concern established in member states under Regulation 1143/2014. Invasive species are a leading cause of biodiversity loss. Data maintained by the European Environment Agency.
global_indicators.15-5-1-intention: Invasive alien species threaten native biodiversity and ecosystem services. Progress means limiting the spread of invasive alien species.
global_indicators.15-5-1-methodology: Data maintained by the EEA based on national monitoring reports under the EU invasive alien species regulation. Published as part of the EU biodiversity monitoring framework.
global_indicators.15-50-title: Area at risk of severe soil erosion by water
global_indicators.15-6-1-title: Number of countries that have adopted legislative, administrative and policy frameworks to ensure fair and equitable sharing of benefits
global_indicators.15-7-1-title: Proportion of traded wildlife that was poached or illicitly trafficked
global_indicators.15-8-1-title: Proportion of countries adopting relevant national legislation and adequately resourcing the prevention or control of invasive alien species
global_indicators.15-9-1-title: (a) Number of countries that have established national targets in accordance with or similar to Aichi Biodiversity Target 2 of the Strategic Plan for Biodiversity 2011–2020 in their national biodiversity strategy and action plans and the progress reported towards these targets; and (b) integration of biodiversity into national accounting and reporting systems, defined as implementation of the System of Environmental-Economic Accounting
global_indicators.15-a-1-title: (a) Official development assistance on conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity; and (b) revenue generated and finance mobilized from biodiversity-relevant economic instruments
global_indicators.15-b-1-title: (a) Official development assistance on conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity; and (b) revenue generated and finance mobilized from biodiversity-relevant economic instruments
global_indicators.15-c-1-title: Proportion of traded wildlife that was poached or illicitly trafficked
global_indicators.16-1-1-definition: Number of intentional homicides per 100,000 inhabitants. Defined as unlawful death inflicted with intent to cause death or serious injury. Data compiled by Eurostat from national criminal justice statistics.
global_indicators.16-1-1-intention: The homicide rate is one of the most reliable measures of violent crime and public safety. Progress means a sustained reduction in intentional homicide rates.
global_indicators.16-1-1-methodology: Data compiled by Eurostat from national police and criminal justice statistics following UNODC definitions. Published annually.
global_indicators.16-1-2-title: Conflict-related deaths per 100,000 population, by sex, age and cause
global_indicators.16-1-3-title: Proportion of population subjected to (a) physical violence, (b) psychological violence and (c) sexual violence in the previous 12 months
global_indicators.16-1-4-title: Proportion of population that feel safe walking alone around the area they live after dark
global_indicators.16-10-1-title: Number of verified cases of killing, kidnapping, enforced disappearance, arbitrary detention and torture of journalists, associated media personnel, trade unionists and human rights advocates in the previous 12 months
global_indicators.16-10-2-title: Number of countries that adopt and implement constitutional, statutory and/or policy guarantees for public access to information
global_indicators.16-10-title: Standardised death rate due to homicid
global_indicators.16-2-1-definition: Perceived level of public sector corruption, scored 0 (highly corrupt) to 100 (very clean). Based on expert assessments and business surveys. Compiled by Transparency International and used in Eurostat SDG monitoring.
global_indicators.16-2-1-intention: Corruption undermines public institutions and sustainable development. Progress means an improving (increasing) corruption perceptions score.
global_indicators.16-2-1-methodology: Compiled annually by Transparency International from multiple expert and business surveys. Scores normalised on a 0–100 scale. Published annually.
global_indicators.16-2-2-title: Number of victims of human trafficking per 100,000 population, by sex, age and form of exploitation
global_indicators.16-2-3-title: Proportion of young women and men aged 18–29 years who experienced sexual violence by age 18
global_indicators.16-20-title: Population reporting crime, violence or vandalism in their are
global_indicators.16-3-1-definition: Proportion of the population reporting experience of crime, violence or vandalism in their local area in the past year. Reflects perceptions of safety. Data collected through EU-SILC.
global_indicators.16-3-1-intention: Feeling safe is a dimension of quality of life. Progress means a reduction in the share of people reporting crime or violence in their area.
global_indicators.16-3-1-methodology: Data collected through EU-SILC. Respondents asked about crime, violence or vandalism experienced in their area. Published annually by Eurostat.
global_indicators.16-3-1-title: Population reporting crime, violence or vandalism in their area
global_indicators.16-3-2-title: Unsentenced detainees as a proportion of overall prison population
global_indicators.16-3-3-title: Proportion of the population who have experienced a dispute in the past two years and who accessed a formal or informal dispute resolution mechanism, by type of mechanism
global_indicators.16-30-title: General government total expenditure on law courts
global_indicators.16-4-1-definition: Number of persons held in prison per 100,000 inhabitants. Reflects criminal justice practices. Data compiled by Eurostat from national penitentiary statistics.
global_indicators.16-4-1-intention: Monitoring prison populations provides insight into criminal justice and rule of law. Imprisonment should be proportionate and consistent with fair justice principles.
global_indicators.16-4-1-methodology: Data compiled from national penitentiary administration statistics. Refers to total persons held on a reference date. Published annually by Eurostat.
global_indicators.16-4-2-title: Proportion of seized, found or surrendered arms whose illicit origin or context has been traced or established by a competent authority in line with international instruments
global_indicators.16-40-title: Perceived independence of the justice system: very or fairly good
global_indicators.16-5-1-definition: Proportion of the population who perceive courts as fairly or very independent. Reflects public trust in judicial institutions and rule of law. Data from EU Justice Scoreboard Eurobarometer surveys.
global_indicators.16-5-1-intention: Trust in judicial independence is fundamental to the rule of law. Progress means an increasing proportion of citizens perceiving justice as independent.
global_indicators.16-5-1-methodology: Data collected through annual Eurobarometer surveys. Respondents assess independence of courts from government and economic interests. Published in the EU Justice Scoreboard.
global_indicators.16-5-1-title: Perceived independence of the justice system
global_indicators.16-5-2-title: Proportion of businesses that had at least one contact with a public official and that paid a bribe to a public official, or were asked for a bribe by those public officials during the previous 12 months
global_indicators.16-6-1-title: Primary government expenditures as a proportion of original approved budget, by sector (or by budget codes or similar)
global_indicators.16-6-2-title: Proportion of population satisfied with their last experience of public services
global_indicators.16-7-1-title: Proportions of positions in national and local institutions, including (a) the legislatures; (b) the public service; and (c) the judiciary, compared to national distributions, by sex, age, persons with disabilities and population groups
global_indicators.16-7-2-title: Proportion of population who believe decision-making is inclusive and responsive, by sex, age, disability and population group
global_indicators.16-70-title: Victims of trafficking in human beings by sex
global_indicators.16-8-1-title: Proportion of members and voting rights of developing countries in international organizations
global_indicators.16-9-1-title: Proportion of children under 5 years of age whose births have been registered with a civil authority, by age
global_indicators.16-a-1-title: Existence of independent national human rights institutions in compliance with the Paris Principles
global_indicators.16-b-1-title: Proportion of population reporting having personally felt discriminated against or harassed in the previous 12 months on the basis of a ground of discrimination prohibited under international human rights law
global_indicators.17-1-1-definition: Net official development assistance (ODA) provided by donor countries as a percentage of gross national income (GNI). The internationally agreed target is 0.7% of GNI. Data compiled by the OECD DAC and Eurostat.
global_indicators.17-1-1-intention: ODA is a key source of development finance for lower-income countries. Progress means an increasing ODA-to-GNI ratio among donor countries.
global_indicators.17-1-1-methodology: Data compiled by the OECD Development Assistance Committee (DAC) and published by Eurostat. Covers bilateral and multilateral flows. Published annually.
global_indicators.17-1-1-title: Official development assistance as share of gross national income
global_indicators.17-1-2-title: Proportion of domestic budget funded by domestic taxes
global_indicators.17-11-1-title: Developing countries’ and least developed countries’ share of global exports
global_indicators.17-12-1-title: Weighted average tariffs faced by developing countries, least developed countries and small island developing States
global_indicators.17-14-1-title: Number of countries with mechanisms in place to enhance policy coherence of sustainable development
global_indicators.17-15-1-title: Extent of use of country-owned results frameworks and planning tools by providers of development cooperation
global_indicators.17-16-1-title: Number of countries reporting progress in multi-stakeholder development effectiveness monitoring frameworks that support the achievement of the sustainable development goals
global_indicators.17-17-1-title: Amount in United States dollars committed to public-private partnerships for infrastructure
global_indicators.17-18-1-title: Statistical capacity indicator for Sustainable Development Goal monitoring
global_indicators.17-18-2-title: Number of countries that have national statistical legislation that complies with the Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics
global_indicators.17-18-3-title: Number of countries with a national statistical plan that is fully funded and under implementation, by source of funding
global_indicators.17-19-1-title: Dollar value of all resources made available to strengthen statistical capacity in developing countries
global_indicators.17-19-2-title: Proportion of countries that (a) have conducted at least one population and housing census in the last 10 years; and (b) have achieved 100 per cent birth registration and 80 per cent death registration
global_indicators.17-2-1-definition: Total tax revenue including social contributions as a percentage of GDP. Reflects the capacity of governments to mobilise domestic resources. Data compiled by Eurostat from national accounts.
global_indicators.17-2-1-intention: Adequate domestic resource mobilisation finances sustainable development. Progress means a stable and sufficient tax revenue base for public services.
global_indicators.17-2-1-methodology: Data compiled from national accounts under ESA 2010. Includes all compulsory levies and social contributions. Published annually by Eurostat.
global_indicators.17-2-1-title: Tax revenue as share of GDP
global_indicators.17-3-1-definition: General government consolidated gross debt as a percentage of GDP. Reflects fiscal sustainability and capacity to finance public investment. Data compiled by Eurostat under the Excessive Deficit Procedure.
global_indicators.17-3-1-intention: Sustainable public finances are essential for long-term development investment. Progress means maintaining debt at levels consistent with fiscal sustainability.
global_indicators.17-3-1-methodology: Data compiled by Eurostat under the Excessive Deficit Procedure (EDP). Published twice yearly for all EU member states and candidate countries.
global_indicators.17-3-1-title: Government debt as share of GDP
global_indicators.17-3-2-title: Volume of remittances (in United States dollars) as a proportion of total GDP
global_indicators.17-31-title: EU imports from least developed countries
global_indicators.17-4-1-definition: Trade openness is measured as total exports plus imports of goods and services as a percentage of GDP. It indicates the degree of integration into the global trading system. Data are compiled from national accounts by Eurostat.
global_indicators.17-4-1-intention: Open trade promotes economic growth and development. Progress means maintaining openness in support of sustainable development goals.
global_indicators.17-4-1-methodology: Data are compiled from national accounts under ESA 2010. Exports and imports cover goods and services. Published annually by Eurostat.
global_indicators.17-5-1-definition: This indicator measures the proportion of individuals using the internet in the last three months, as a percentage of total population. Data are collected through the EU ICT Usage Survey.
global_indicators.17-5-1-intention: Internet access enables participation in the digital economy and access to information. Progress means a growing share of the population using the internet regularly.
global_indicators.17-5-1-methodology: Data are collected through the annual EU Survey on ICT Usage in Households and by Individuals. Published annually by Eurostat.
global_indicators.17-5-1-title: Internet users as share of population

global_indicators.17-6-2-title: Fixed Internet broadband subscriptions per 100 inhabitants, by speed
global_indicators.17-60-title: Share of households with high-speed internet connection
global_indicators.17-7-1-title: Total amount of funding for developing countries to promote the development, transfer, dissemination and diffusion of environmentally sound technologies
global_indicators.17-8-1-title: Proportion of individuals using the Internet
global_indicators.17-9-1-title: Dollar value of financial and technical assistance (including through North-South, South‐South and triangular cooperation) committed to developing countries
global_indicators.2-1-1-definition: The consumer food price index measures changes over time in the prices paid by consumers for food and non-alcoholic beverages. It is expressed as an index with a reference period equal to 100. Rising food prices can increase food insecurity, particularly among lower-income households. Data are compiled by Eurostat from national statistical authorities.
global_indicators.2-1-1-intention: Stable and affordable food prices are essential for ensuring access to adequate nutrition for all segments of the population. Sharp price increases disproportionately affect lower-income households and can push people into food insecurity. Monitoring this indicator contributes to the broader goal of ending hunger.
global_indicators.2-1-1-methodology: Data are based on the Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) food sub-index, collected monthly by national statistical authorities using standardised Eurostat methodology. The index covers all food and non-alcoholic beverages following the COICOP classification.
global_indicators.2-1-2-title: Prevalence of moderate or severe food insecurity in the population, based on the Food Insecurity Experience Scale (FIES)
global_indicators.2-10-title: Obesity rate by body mass index (BMI)
global_indicators.2-2-1-definition: This indicator measures the proportion of adults aged 18 and over classified as overweight or obese based on Body Mass Index (BMI). Overweight is defined as BMI ≥ 25 kg/m² and obesity as BMI ≥ 30 kg/m². It is expressed as a percentage of the adult population. Data are collected through the European Health Interview Survey (EHIS).
global_indicators.2-2-1-intention: Overweight and obesity are major risk factors for non-communicable diseases including cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes and certain cancers. Rising obesity rates place significant burdens on healthcare systems and reduce healthy life expectancy. Progress means stabilising or reducing the prevalence of overweight and obesity.
global_indicators.2-2-1-methodology: Data are collected through the European Health Interview Survey (EHIS), conducted approximately every five years. BMI is calculated from self-reported height and weight. EHIS follows a harmonised methodology across all participating countries, enabling cross-country comparisons.
global_indicators.2-2-1-title: Overweight and obesity rate in adults
global_indicators.2-2-2-title: Prevalence of malnutrition (weight for height >+2 or <-2 standard deviation from the median of the WHO Child Growth Standards) among children under 5 years of age, by type (wasting and overweight)
global_indicators.2-2-3-title: Prevalence of anaemia in women aged 15 to 49 years, by pregnancy status (percentage)
global_indicators.2-20-title: Agricultural real factor income per annual work unit (AWU)
global_indicators.2-3-1-definition: The farmland bird index measures changes in the population of bird species associated with farmland habitats, using 1990 as the base year (index = 100). A decline in farmland bird populations indicates biodiversity loss driven by agricultural intensification. Data are collected from national bird monitoring schemes.
global_indicators.2-3-1-intention: The diversity of bird populations in agricultural landscapes is an indicator of the ecological health of farming systems. Stable or increasing bird populations signal that agricultural practices support biodiversity. Halting and reversing the decline in farmland bird populations is essential for sustainable food systems.
global_indicators.2-3-1-methodology: Data are compiled from national breeding bird surveys and reported to Eurostat. The index aggregates population trends across a representative set of bird species typical of farmland habitats. Results are smoothed to account for year-to-year variability in survey counts.
global_indicators.2-3-2-title: Average income of small-scale food producers, by sex and indigenous status
global_indicators.2-30-title: Government support to agricultural research and development
global_indicators.2-4-1-definition: This indicator measures the total agricultural area under organic farming, including both fully certified organic land and land currently in the conversion period. It is expressed as a percentage of the total utilised agricultural area (UAA). Data are based on national organic farming statistics compiled by Eurostat.
global_indicators.2-4-1-intention: Organic farming promotes biodiversity, reduces the use of synthetic pesticides and fertilisers, and supports sustainable soil and water management. Increasing the share of organic farmland is an important step towards more sustainable and resilient food production systems.
global_indicators.2-4-1-methodology: Data are collected through national farm surveys and agricultural statistics, compiled in accordance with EU organic farming regulations. Figures include land fully certified as organic as well as land in the conversion period, typically lasting two to three years.
global_indicators.2-5-1-title: Number of plant and animal genetic resources for food and agriculture secured in either medium- or long-term conservation facilities
global_indicators.2-5-2-title: Proportion of local breeds classified as being at risk of extinction
global_indicators.2-5-3-definition: The gross nitrogen balance (GNB) on agricultural land estimates the nitrogen surplus in the soil, calculated as the difference between nitrogen inputs (mineral fertilisers, manure, atmospheric deposition, biological fixation and crop residues) and outputs (crops and grass harvested). It is expressed in kilograms of nitrogen per hectare of agricultural land.
global_indicators.2-5-3-intention: Excess nitrogen in agricultural soils contributes to water pollution through nitrate leaching, greenhouse gas emissions and biodiversity loss. Reducing the nitrogen surplus is essential for sustainable agricultural practices that protect water bodies and the broader environment.
global_indicators.2-5-3-methodology: Data are compiled by Eurostat from national agricultural statistics on fertiliser use, livestock numbers and crop production. The GNB methodology follows the OECD/Eurostat approach for nutrient balance calculation and is updated annually.
global_indicators.2-5-3-title: Gross nitrogen balance on agricultural land
global_indicators.2-53-title: Use and risk of chemical pesticides
global_indicators.2-6-0-definition: This indicator measures total greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from the agricultural sector, expressed in million tonnes of CO₂ equivalent. Agricultural emissions include methane from livestock and manure management, nitrous oxide from soils and carbon dioxide from on-farm energy use.
global_indicators.2-6-0-intention: Agriculture contributes significantly to total greenhouse gas emissions. Reducing agricultural emissions while maintaining food production is a key challenge for meeting climate targets. Progress means a reduction in total GHG emissions from agriculture without compromising food security.
global_indicators.2-6-0-methodology: Data are reported by national authorities under the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and compiled by Eurostat. Emissions are estimated using IPCC methodology and cover all agricultural emission sources including enteric fermentation, manure management and agricultural soils.
global_indicators.2-a-1-title: The agriculture orientation index for government expenditures
global_indicators.2-a-2-title: Total official flows (official development assistance plus other official flows) to the agriculture sector
global_indicators.3-1-1-definition: Healthy life years (HLY) at birth indicate the number of years a newborn is expected to live in good health, free from long-standing illness or disability. HLY are calculated by combining age-specific mortality rates with age-specific proportions of people reporting a limiting long-standing illness. The indicator is expressed in years and disaggregated by sex.
global_indicators.3-1-1-intention: Healthy life years go beyond life expectancy by measuring the quality as well as the length of life. Increasing HLY means people not only live longer but spend more years in good health. Progress means a sustained increase in healthy life years for both men and women.
global_indicators.3-1-1-methodology: HLY are calculated using the Sullivan method, combining mortality data with self-reported disability data from EU-SILC. The global activity limitation indicator (GALI) asks whether respondents have been limited in activities due to health problems for at least six months.
global_indicators.3-1-2-title: Proportion of births attended by skilled health personnel
global_indicators.3-12-title: Healthy life years based on self-perceived health (previous: Healthy life years at birth)
global_indicators.3-2-1-definition: The under-five mortality rate is the probability that a child born in a given year will die before reaching the age of five, expressed per 1,000 live births. It reflects the cumulative effect of multiple determinants of child survival including nutrition, healthcare access, sanitation and living conditions. Data are compiled from national vital statistics.
global_indicators.3-2-1-intention: Reducing child mortality is a fundamental measure of human development and of the effectiveness of health and social systems. High under-five mortality rates reflect inadequate healthcare access and poor living conditions. Progress means a steady reduction in preventable deaths among children under five.
global_indicators.3-2-1-methodology: Data are compiled from national civil registration and vital statistics systems. The rate is calculated from age-specific death rates for children under five. Eurostat compiles and validates data from national statistical authorities following harmonised definitions.
global_indicators.3-20-title: Share of people with good or very good perceived health by sex
global_indicators.3-3-1-definition: This indicator measures the proportion of adults aged 15 and over who currently smoke tobacco products (including cigarettes, cigars and pipes) on a daily or occasional basis. It is expressed as a percentage of the total adult population. Data are collected through the European Health Interview Survey (EHIS).
global_indicators.3-3-1-intention: Tobacco use is the leading preventable cause of death globally, causing cancer, cardiovascular disease and chronic respiratory conditions. Reducing smoking prevalence is a key public health priority. Progress means a sustained decline in the proportion of adults who smoke.
global_indicators.3-3-1-methodology: Data are collected through the European Health Interview Survey (EHIS), conducted approximately every five years. Smoking status is self-reported. The survey uses a standardised questionnaire enabling cross-country comparisons across all EU member states and participating countries.
global_indicators.3-3-5-title: Number of people requiring interventions against neglected tropical diseases
global_indicators.3-4-1-definition: This indicator measures the standardised death rate from non-communicable chronic diseases, including cardiovascular diseases, cancer, diabetes and chronic respiratory diseases. It is expressed as deaths per 100,000 persons, standardised to the European Standard Population (ESP 2013). Data are compiled by Eurostat from national causes of death statistics.
global_indicators.3-4-1-intention: Non-communicable diseases are the leading cause of premature mortality in Europe. Reducing premature deaths from chronic diseases requires effective prevention, early detection and access to quality healthcare. Progress means a reduction in the standardised death rate from these diseases over time.
global_indicators.3-4-1-methodology: Data are based on causes of death statistics from national death registries. The standardised death rate eliminates the effect of different age structures when comparing populations, using the European Standard Population (ESP 2013) as the reference. Data are reported annually to Eurostat.
global_indicators.3-4-1-title: Standardised death rate from chronic diseases
global_indicators.3-5-1-title: Coverage of treatment interventions (pharmacological, psychosocial and rehabilitation and aftercare services) for substance use disorders
global_indicators.3-5-2-title: Alcohol per capita consumption (aged 15 years and older) within a calendar year in litres of pure alcohol
global_indicators.3-6-1-definition: This indicator measures the number of persons killed in road traffic accidents per million inhabitants. A person is classified as a road traffic fatality if they die within 30 days of the accident as a result of injuries sustained. Data are compiled by Eurostat from national road safety databases.
global_indicators.3-6-1-intention: Road traffic injuries are a leading cause of death, particularly among young people. Reducing fatalities requires investment in infrastructure, vehicle safety standards, speed management and enforcement of traffic laws. Progress means a significant and sustained reduction in road deaths per million inhabitants.
global_indicators.3-6-1-methodology: Data are compiled from national road traffic accident databases. The 30-day fatality definition was standardised to harmonise counting across participating countries. Data are reported annually to Eurostat and verified against population statistics from national sources.
global_indicators.3-60-title: Self-reported unmet need for medical examination and care by sex
global_indicators.3-7-1-definition: The adolescent birth rate is the number of live births per 1,000 women aged 15 to 19 years. It measures the prevalence of teenage pregnancies and reflects access to sexual and reproductive health education and services. Data are compiled from national vital statistics by Eurostat.
global_indicators.3-7-1-intention: High adolescent birth rates are associated with increased health risks for mother and child, and with reduced educational and economic opportunities for young women. Reducing the adolescent birth rate requires access to comprehensive sexual education and reproductive health services. Progress means a sustained decrease in births to adolescent women.
global_indicators.3-7-1-methodology: Data are compiled from national birth registrations and population statistics. The rate is calculated by dividing live births to women aged 15–19 by the total female population aged 15–19, multiplied by 1,000. Data are reported to Eurostat annually by national statistical authorities.
global_indicators.3-7-2-title: Adolescent birth rate (aged 10–14 years; aged 15–19 years) per 1,000 women in that age group
global_indicators.3-70-title: Consumption of antibiotics in the community and hospital sectors – defined daily doses (DDD) per day
global_indicators.3-8-2-title: Proportion of population with large household expenditures on health as a share of total household expenditure or income
global_indicators.3-9-1-title: Mortality rate attributed to household and ambient air pollution
global_indicators.3-9-2-title: Mortality rate attributed to unsafe water, unsafe sanitation and lack of hygiene (exposure to unsafe Water, Sanitation and Hygiene for All (WASH) services)
global_indicators.3-9-3-title: Mortality rate attributed to unintentional poisoning
global_indicators.3-a-1-title: Age-standardized prevalence of current tobacco use among persons aged 15 years and older
global_indicators.3-b-1-title: Proportion of the target population covered by all vaccines included in their national programme
global_indicators.3-b-2-title: Total net official development assistance to medical research and basic health sectors
global_indicators.3-b-3-title: Proportion of health facilities that have a core set of relevant essential medicines available and affordable on a sustainable basis
global_indicators.3-d-1-title: International Health Regulations (IHR) capacity and health emergency preparedness
global_indicators.3-d-2-title: Percentage of bloodstream infections due to selected antimicrobial-resistant organisms
global_indicators.4-1-1-definition: Early leavers from education and training are persons aged 18 to 24 who have attained at most lower secondary education and are not in further education or training. The indicator is expressed as a percentage of the total population aged 18 to 24. Data are based on the EU Labour Force Survey.
global_indicators.4-1-1-intention: Reducing early school leaving is essential for ensuring that all young people acquire the knowledge and skills needed for employment and active citizenship. High rates of early leaving are associated with lower earning potential, higher unemployment, and greater dependence on social support systems. The long-term objective is to minimise the share of early leavers.
