global_indicators.4-1-1-methodology: Data are collected through the EU Labour Force Survey (EU-LFS), a large household survey providing quarterly statistics on labour participation. The indicator covers persons aged 18 to 24 whose highest level of education is ISCED 2011 level 0, 1 or 2, and who stated they had not received any education or training in the four weeks preceding the survey.
global_indicators.4-1-1-title: Early leavers from education and training
global_indicators.4-1-2-title: Completion rate (primary education, lower secondary education, upper secondary education)
global_indicators.4-10-title: Early leavers from education and training by sex
global_indicators.4-2-1-definition: This indicator measures the proportion of persons aged 25 to 34 who have successfully completed tertiary education (ISCED 2011 levels 5–8). It is expressed as a percentage of the total population in that age group. Data are based on the EU Labour Force Survey.
global_indicators.4-2-1-intention: Increasing tertiary educational attainment is key to developing a skilled workforce capable of driving innovation and economic growth. Higher levels of education are associated with better employment prospects, higher earnings and greater civic participation. Progress means a sustained rise in the share of young people completing tertiary education.
global_indicators.4-2-1-methodology: Data are collected through the EU Labour Force Survey (EU-LFS). Tertiary education corresponds to ISCED 2011 levels 5 to 8, covering short-cycle tertiary education, bachelor's or equivalent, master's or equivalent, and doctoral or equivalent programmes. The age group 25–34 is chosen because most people in this range have completed their initial education.
global_indicators.4-2-2-title: Participation rate in organized learning (one year before the official primary entry age), by sex
global_indicators.4-3-1-definition: This indicator measures the proportion of children aged 3 years to the starting age of compulsory education who participate in early childhood education programmes. It is expressed as a percentage of the population in the same age group. Data are collected from national administrative sources.
global_indicators.4-3-1-intention: Early childhood education is key to preparing children for primary school and life-long learning. High participation rates reduce inequalities and support cognitive, emotional and social development from an early age. The long-term goal is to maximise participation of all children in quality early education.
global_indicators.4-3-1-methodology: Data are compiled by Eurostat from national administrative sources and refer to children enrolled in ISCED 2011 level 0 (early childhood education) programmes. Coverage includes both public and private institutions. The reference population is children aged 3 years to the starting age of compulsory education.
global_indicators.4-31-title: Participation in early childhood education by sex (children aged 3 and over)
global_indicators.4-4-1-definition: This indicator measures the share of 15-year-old students who fail to reach level 2 (minimum level of proficiency) in reading, mathematics and science, based on the OECD Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA). It is expressed as a percentage of all students assessed.
global_indicators.4-4-1-intention: Ensuring that all young people acquire minimum literacy and numeracy skills is fundamental to quality education. High rates of underachievement limit future employment and economic participation. Progress means reducing the share of low-achieving students in all three domains.
global_indicators.4-4-1-methodology: Data come from the OECD PISA survey, conducted every three years among students aged 15. Level 2 proficiency is the baseline level at which students begin to demonstrate competencies that enable them to participate actively in modern society. The survey covers reading, mathematics and science.
global_indicators.4-4-1-title: Low achieving students in reading, mathematics and science
global_indicators.4-40-title: Low achieving 15-year-olds in reading, mathematics or science
global_indicators.4-5-1-definition: This indicator measures the proportion of individuals aged 16 to 74 who possess at least basic digital skills across four areas: information and data literacy, communication and collaboration, problem solving, and digital content creation. It is expressed as a percentage of the total population aged 16 to 74.
global_indicators.4-5-1-intention: Digital skills are increasingly essential for participation in the labour market and in society. Ensuring a digitally competent population supports economic growth, innovation and social inclusion. Progress means increasing the share of people with at least basic digital competences.
global_indicators.4-5-1-methodology: Data are collected through the EU Survey on ICT Usage in Households and by Individuals. The composite digital skills indicator is based on the EU Digital Competence Framework (DigComp) and covers activities performed in the 3 months prior to the survey.
global_indicators.4-5-1-title: Individuals with at least basic digital skills
global_indicators.4-6-1-definition: This indicator measures the proportion of adults aged 25 to 64 who participated in formal or non-formal education and training in the four weeks preceding the survey. It is expressed as a percentage of the total population aged 25 to 64. Data are based on the EU Labour Force Survey.
global_indicators.4-6-1-intention: Life-long learning is essential for adapting to a changing labour market and maintaining employability. Higher participation in adult learning reduces skills mismatches and supports social inclusion. The goal is to increase the proportion of adults engaged in continuous learning throughout their lives.
global_indicators.4-6-1-methodology: Data are collected through the EU Labour Force Survey (EU-LFS). Formal education refers to education provided by the regular system of schools, universities and other formal educational institutions. Non-formal education includes all organised educational activities outside the formal educational system.
global_indicators.4-60-title: Adult participation in learning in the past four weeks by sex
global_indicators.4-7-1-title: Extent to which (i) global citizenship education and (ii) education for sustainable development are mainstreamed in (a) national education policies; (b) curricula; (c) teacher education; and (d) student assessment
global_indicators.4-70-title: Share of individuals having at least basic digital skills, by sex
global_indicators.4-a-1-title: Proportion of schools offering basic services, by type of service
global_indicators.4-b-1-title: Volume of official development assistance flows for scholarships by sector and type of study
global_indicators.4-c-1-title: Proportion of teachers with the minimum required qualifications, by education level
global_indicators.5-1-1-definition: The gender employment gap is the difference between the employment rates of men and women aged 20 to 64, expressed in percentage points. A positive value indicates that men have a higher employment rate than women. Data are based on the EU Labour Force Survey (EU-LFS).
global_indicators.5-1-1-intention: The gender employment gap reflects structural inequalities in the labour market. Closing the gap requires policies supporting women's participation in employment, including affordable childcare, flexible working arrangements and equal opportunities. Progress means a sustained reduction in the difference between men's and women's employment rates.
global_indicators.5-1-1-methodology: Data are collected through the EU Labour Force Survey (EU-LFS). The employment rate is calculated as the percentage of employed persons in the total population aged 20–64. The gender employment gap is the difference between the male and female employment rates, expressed in percentage points.
global_indicators.5-10-title: Physical and sexual violence to women by age group (2012 data)
global_indicators.5-2-1-definition: The unadjusted gender pay gap is the difference between average gross hourly earnings of male and female employees, expressed as a percentage of average gross hourly earnings of male employees. It is based on employees working in firms with ten or more employees. Data are collected through the Structure of Earnings Survey (SES).
global_indicators.5-2-1-intention: The gender pay gap reflects persistent inequalities between men and women in the labour market, including differences in sectors, occupations, working hours and career interruptions. Closing the gap requires addressing occupational segregation and discrimination. Progress means a sustained reduction in the unadjusted gender pay gap over time.
global_indicators.5-2-1-methodology: Data are collected through the Structure of Earnings Survey (SES), conducted every four years, with annual estimates produced by Eurostat. The indicator covers all economic activities except public administration and is based on gross hourly earnings of employees in establishments with ten or more employees.
global_indicators.5-2-2-title: Proportion of women and girls aged 15 years and older subjected to sexual violence by persons other than an intimate partner in the previous 12 months, by age and place of occurrence
global_indicators.5-20-title: Gender pay gap in unadjusted form
global_indicators.5-3-1-definition: The gender pension gap is the difference between the average pension income received by men and women aged 65 to 79, expressed as a percentage of the average pension income received by men. It reflects accumulated inequalities from the labour market, including differences in employment rates, working hours, pay and career breaks. Data are based on EU-SILC.
global_indicators.5-3-1-intention: The gender pension gap is a consequence of lifetime inequalities in employment and earnings between men and women. Closing the gap requires addressing the root causes throughout working life, including career breaks for care responsibilities, part-time work and occupational segregation. Progress means a sustained reduction in the pension income gap between men and women.
global_indicators.5-3-1-methodology: Data are collected through the EU Statistics on Income and Living Conditions (EU-SILC). Pension income includes old-age and survivors' pensions. The gender pension gap is calculated as the difference between average male and female pension incomes, expressed as a percentage of average male pension income, for persons aged 65 to 79.
global_indicators.5-3-2-title: Proportion of girls and women aged 15–49 years who have undergone female genital mutilation/cutting, by age
global_indicators.5-30-title: Gender employment gap, by type of employment
global_indicators.5-4-1-definition: This indicator measures the proportion of women among members of boards of directors of the largest publicly listed companies, expressed as a percentage of all board members. It covers both executive and non-executive board members. Data are collected by Eurostat in cooperation with the European Institute for Gender Equality (EIGE).
global_indicators.5-4-1-intention: Women remain underrepresented in senior decision-making positions in the corporate sector. Increasing the share of women on company boards promotes gender equality and is associated with better governance and business performance. Progress means a sustained increase in the proportion of women in board-level positions.
global_indicators.5-4-1-methodology: Data are collected from national sources by Eurostat in cooperation with EIGE. The indicator covers the largest publicly listed companies registered in each country, specifically those listed on each country's main national stock exchange. Board members include both supervisory and management board members.
global_indicators.5-4-1-title: Women on boards of large listed companies
global_indicators.5-40-title: Persons outside the labour force due to caring responsibilities by sex
global_indicators.5-5-1-definition: This indicator measures the proportion of seats held by women in national parliaments (single or lower chamber), expressed as a percentage of all occupied seats. Data are provided by the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) and compiled by Eurostat.
global_indicators.5-5-1-intention: Equal participation of women and men in political decision-making is a fundamental dimension of gender equality and democratic governance. Increasing women's representation in parliament ensures that women's perspectives and interests are reflected in legislation and policy. Progress means an increasing share of seats held by women.
global_indicators.5-5-1-methodology: Data are provided by the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) and refer to the situation on 1 January of each year. The indicator covers single chambers and the lower chambers of bicameral parliaments. Figures refer to the percentage of women among all members of parliament with a valid mandate.
global_indicators.5-5-1-title: Seats held by women in national parliaments
global_indicators.5-5-2-title: Proportion of women in managerial positions
global_indicators.5-50-title: Seats held by women in national parliaments and governments
global_indicators.5-6-1-definition: This indicator measures the difference between the proportion of men and women aged 16 to 74 who used the internet in the last three months, expressed in percentage points. A positive value indicates higher internet use among men. Data are collected through the EU Survey on ICT Usage in Households and by Individuals.
global_indicators.5-6-1-intention: The digital gender gap reflects broader inequalities in access to technology, information and economic opportunities. Closing the gap requires targeted policies to improve digital access, skills and confidence among women. Progress means a reduction in the difference between male and female internet use rates.
global_indicators.5-6-1-methodology: Data are collected through the EU Survey on ICT Usage in Households and by Individuals, conducted annually. Internet use refers to use of the internet for any purpose in the three months preceding the survey. The gender gap is calculated as the difference between male and female internet use rates, expressed in percentage points.
global_indicators.5-6-2-title: Number of countries with laws and regulations that guarantee full and equal access to women and men aged 15 years and older to sexual and reproductive health care, information and education
global_indicators.5-60-title: Positions held by women in senior management positions
global_indicators.5-a-1-title: (a) Proportion of total agricultural population with ownership or secure rights over agricultural land, by sex; and (b) share of women among owners or rights-bearers of agricultural land, by type of tenure
global_indicators.5-a-2-title: Proportion of countries where the legal framework (including customary law) guarantees women’s equal rights to land ownership and/or control
global_indicators.5-b-1-title: Proportion of individuals who own a mobile telephone, by sex
global_indicators.5-c-1-title: Proportion of countries with systems to track and make public allocations for gender equality and women’s empowerment
global_indicators.6-1-1-definition: The water exploitation index (WEI+) measures freshwater abstraction as a proportion of the available renewable freshwater resources (long-term average annual renewable freshwater resources minus environmental flow requirements). It is expressed as a percentage. Values above 20% indicate water stress; above 40% indicate severe water stress.
global_indicators.6-1-1-intention: Water scarcity is an increasing threat to ecosystems, economies and human well-being. Monitoring freshwater abstraction relative to available resources is essential for sustainable water management. Progress means maintaining the water exploitation index below stress thresholds through efficient water use and resource management.
global_indicators.6-1-1-methodology: Data are compiled by Eurostat from national water statistics reported by member states. Freshwater abstraction covers water withdrawn from rivers, lakes, reservoirs and groundwater for all uses. Available resources are estimated from long-term hydrological data adjusted for environmental flow requirements.
global_indicators.6-2-1-definition: This indicator measures the proportion of the population whose wastewater is collected and treated in urban wastewater treatment plants, expressed as a percentage. It covers at least secondary (biological) treatment. Data are reported by member states under the Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive and compiled by Eurostat.
global_indicators.6-2-1-intention: Access to adequate wastewater treatment is fundamental for protecting water quality and public health. Untreated wastewater contaminates rivers, lakes and coastal waters. Progress means an increasing proportion of the population connected to at least secondary wastewater treatment.
global_indicators.6-2-1-methodology: Data are reported by member states every two years under Council Directive 91/271/EEC concerning urban wastewater treatment. The indicator covers agglomerations generating more than 2,000 population equivalents. Eurostat compiles and publishes the data as a percentage of the total population.
global_indicators.6-2-1-title: Population connected to urban wastewater treatment
global_indicators.6-20-title: Population connected to at least secondary wastewater treatment
global_indicators.6-3-1-definition: This indicator measures the biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) in rivers, which reflects the amount of oxygen consumed by biological processes when decomposing organic matter in water. Lower BOD values indicate better water quality. It is expressed in milligrams of oxygen per litre and is based on data from river monitoring stations.
global_indicators.6-3-1-intention: High levels of organic pollution in rivers reduce dissolved oxygen, harm aquatic life and can render water unsafe for human use. Reducing BOD in rivers is essential for improving water quality and protecting freshwater ecosystems. Progress means a reduction in average BOD levels across monitored river stations.
global_indicators.6-3-1-methodology: Data are collected from national river monitoring networks and compiled by Eurostat in cooperation with the European Environment Agency (EEA). BOD is measured at standardised monitoring stations and represents the oxygen consumed over five days at 20°C (BOD5). Data are reported annually.
global_indicators.6-3-2-title: Proportion of bodies of water with good ambient water quality
global_indicators.6-4-1-definition: This indicator measures the proportion of groundwater monitoring stations where the average nitrate concentration exceeds 50 milligrams per litre (the EU threshold under the Nitrates Directive). It is expressed as a percentage of all monitored stations. Data are reported by member states under the Nitrates Directive.
global_indicators.6-4-1-intention: Nitrate pollution of groundwater, primarily from agricultural sources, poses risks to drinking water quality and aquatic ecosystems. Reducing nitrate concentrations requires improved agricultural nutrient management. Progress means a reduction in the proportion of monitoring stations exceeding the 50 mg/l threshold.
global_indicators.6-4-1-methodology: Data are collected by member states under Council Directive 91/676/EEC concerning the protection of waters against pollution caused by nitrates from agricultural sources (Nitrates Directive) and reported to the European Commission every four years. Eurostat compiles and publishes the data.
global_indicators.6-4-2-title: Level of water stress: freshwater withdrawal as a proportion of available freshwater resources
global_indicators.6-5-1-definition: This indicator measures the proportion of surface water bodies (rivers, lakes, transitional and coastal waters) achieving good or high ecological status or potential, as defined by the EU Water Framework Directive. It is expressed as a percentage of all assessed water bodies. Data are reported by member states every six years.
global_indicators.6-5-1-intention: The ecological status of water bodies reflects the overall health of aquatic ecosystems and the pressures they face from human activities. Achieving good ecological status is the central objective of the Water Framework Directive. Progress means an increasing proportion of surface water bodies achieving good or high ecological status.
global_indicators.6-5-1-methodology: Data are reported by EU member states to the European Environment Agency (EEA) under the Water Framework Directive (2000/60/EC). Ecological status is assessed based on biological, hydromorphological and physico-chemical quality elements. Reporting cycles run every six years.
global_indicators.6-5-1-title: Water bodies with good ecological status
global_indicators.6-5-2-title: Proportion of transboundary basin area with an operational arrangement for water cooperation
global_indicators.6-6-1-title: Change in the extent of water-related ecosystems over time
global_indicators.6-a-1-title: Amount of water- and sanitation-related official development assistance that is part of a government-coordinated spending plan
global_indicators.6-b-1-title: Proportion of local administrative units with established and operational policies and procedures for participation of local communities in water and sanitation management
global_indicators.7-1-1-definition: Energy productivity measures how much economic output is generated per unit of energy consumed. It is calculated as GDP divided by gross inland energy consumption and expressed in euros per kilogram of oil equivalent (EUR/kgoe). A higher value indicates more efficient use of energy to generate economic output.
global_indicators.7-1-1-intention: Improving energy productivity is central to decoupling economic growth from energy consumption and reducing environmental pressures. More productive use of energy lowers costs for businesses and households and reduces emissions. Progress means a sustained increase in energy productivity over time.
global_indicators.7-1-1-methodology: Energy productivity is calculated by Eurostat using GDP data (chain-linked volumes, reference year 2010) and gross inland energy consumption from national energy balances. Both indicators are compiled under EU energy statistics regulations. Data are published annually.
global_indicators.7-1-2-title: Proportion of population with primary reliance on clean fuels and technology
global_indicators.7-2-1-definition: This indicator measures the share of energy from renewable sources (wind, solar, hydro, geothermal, ocean, biomass and biofuels) in gross final energy consumption, expressed as a percentage. It covers renewable energy used in electricity, heating and cooling, and transport. Data are compiled by Eurostat from national energy statistics.
global_indicators.7-2-1-intention: Increasing the share of renewable energy is essential for reducing greenhouse gas emissions from the energy sector and achieving climate targets. Renewables also contribute to energy security and long-term cost reductions. Progress means a sustained increase in the renewable energy share in total energy consumption.
global_indicators.7-2-1-methodology: Data are compiled by Eurostat from national energy statistics reported under Directive 2009/28/EC (Renewable Energy Directive) and its successor Directive 2018/2001/EU. Gross final energy consumption includes energy delivered to end users plus grid losses in electricity and distribution losses in heat networks.
global_indicators.7-2-1-title: Share of renewable energy in gross final energy consumption
global_indicators.7-20-title: Final energy consumption in households per capita
global_indicators.7-3-1-definition: Primary energy consumption measures the total energy demand of a country, covering consumption of all energy forms before any transformation process. It is expressed in million tonnes of oil equivalent (Mtoe). It includes energy used by the energy sector, distribution losses and final consumption by all sectors.
global_indicators.7-3-1-intention: Reducing primary energy consumption while maintaining economic output is key to improving energy efficiency and meeting climate targets. Decoupling economic growth from energy consumption is central to sustainable development. Progress means a declining trend in primary energy consumption relative to economic output.
global_indicators.7-3-1-methodology: Data are compiled by Eurostat from national energy balances submitted under EU energy statistics regulations (Regulation EC No 1099/2008). Primary energy consumption is calculated using the substitution method for nuclear and renewable electricity. Data are published annually.
global_indicators.7-4-1-definition: Final energy consumption measures the total energy consumed by end users (industry, transport, households, services and agriculture), excluding energy used by the energy sector itself. It is expressed in million tonnes of oil equivalent (Mtoe) and serves as a key indicator of energy demand. Data are compiled by Eurostat from national energy balances.
global_indicators.7-4-1-intention: Reducing final energy consumption is essential for meeting climate targets and improving energy security. Energy efficiency improvements allow economic growth to decouple from energy use. Progress means a sustained reduction in final energy consumption while maintaining economic activity.
global_indicators.7-4-1-methodology: Data are compiled by Eurostat from national energy balances reported under EU energy statistics regulations. Final energy consumption excludes non-energy use and energy consumed by the energy transformation sector. Data are reported annually in tonnes of oil equivalent.
global_indicators.7-40-title: Share of renewable energy in gross final energy consumption
global_indicators.7-5-1-definition: The energy import dependency rate shows the extent to which an economy relies on energy imports to meet its energy needs. It is calculated as net energy imports divided by gross inland energy consumption, expressed as a percentage. A higher rate means greater dependence on imported energy.
global_indicators.7-5-1-intention: High energy import dependency exposes economies to energy supply disruptions and price volatility. Reducing dependency through energy efficiency and renewable energy development supports energy security and sustainability. Progress means a reduction in the energy import dependency rate.
global_indicators.7-5-1-methodology: Data are compiled by Eurostat from national energy statistics submitted under EU energy statistics regulations. Gross inland energy consumption covers all energy needed to meet domestic demand. Net imports are calculated as imports minus exports and stock changes.
global_indicators.7-6-1-definition: This indicator measures the proportion of the population that is unable to keep their home adequately warm, as a share of total population. It is one of the key indicators of energy poverty in Europe. Data are collected through the EU Statistics on Income and Living Conditions (EU-SILC).
global_indicators.7-6-1-intention: Energy poverty affects health, well-being and quality of life, particularly for low-income households. Ensuring that all people can afford to heat their homes is a fundamental dimension of affordable and clean energy. Progress means a sustained reduction in the share of the population experiencing energy poverty.
global_indicators.7-6-1-methodology: Data are collected through EU-SILC, which asks respondents whether they can afford to keep their home adequately warm. The indicator is expressed as a percentage of the total population. Data are collected annually and published by Eurostat.
global_indicators.7-6-1-title: Population unable to keep home adequately warm
global_indicators.7-60-title: Population unable to keep home adequately warm
global_indicators.7-a-1-title: International financial flows to developing countries in support of clean energy research and development and renewable energy production, including in hybrid systems
global_indicators.7-b-1-title: Installed renewable energy-generating capacity in developing countries (in watts per capita)
global_indicators.8-1-1-definition: Real GDP per capita is gross domestic product at market prices divided by the mid-year population, expressed in chain-linked volumes. It is the most commonly used indicator of economic output and living standards. Growth rates reflect economic performance adjusted for inflation. Data are compiled by Eurostat from national accounts.
global_indicators.8-1-1-intention: Sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth is essential for reducing poverty and improving living standards. Real GDP per capita growth reflects improvements in productivity and economic well-being. Progress means a positive and sustained growth rate in real GDP per capita.
global_indicators.8-1-1-methodology: Data are compiled from national accounts under the European System of Accounts (ESA 2010). Real GDP uses chain-linked volume measures to remove price effects. Per capita figures use mid-year population estimates. Data are published annually by Eurostat.
global_indicators.8-10-1-title: (a) Number of commercial bank branches per 100,000 adults and (b) number of automated teller machines (ATMs) per 100,000 adults
global_indicators.8-10-2-title: Proportion of adults (15 years and older) with an account at a bank or other financial institution or with a mobile-money-service provider
global_indicators.8-2-1-definition: This indicator measures gross fixed capital formation (investment in physical assets such as machinery, buildings and infrastructure) as a percentage of GDP. It reflects the level of investment in the economy and its capacity for future growth. Data are compiled by Eurostat from national accounts.
global_indicators.8-2-1-intention: Investment in physical capital is a key driver of productivity growth and long-term economic development. Adequate investment levels support innovation, job creation and infrastructure improvements. Progress means maintaining or increasing the investment share of GDP at levels consistent with sustainable growth.
global_indicators.8-2-1-methodology: Data are compiled from national accounts reported under the European System of Accounts (ESA 2010). Gross fixed capital formation covers acquisitions of fixed assets minus disposals by resident producers. Data are published annually by Eurostat.
global_indicators.8-2-1-title: Gross fixed capital formation as share of GDP
global_indicators.8-20-title: Young people neither in employment nor in education and training
global_indicators.8-3-1-definition: The employment rate is the proportion of persons aged 20 to 64 who are in employment, expressed as a percentage of the total population in that age group. It is one of the most widely used indicators of labour market performance. Data are based on the EU Labour Force Survey (EU-LFS).
global_indicators.8-3-1-intention: A high employment rate is central to economic prosperity, social inclusion and the sustainability of social protection systems. Increasing employment requires policies supporting job creation, skills development and removing barriers to participation. Progress means a sustained increase in the employment rate.
global_indicators.8-3-1-methodology: Data are collected through the EU Labour Force Survey (EU-LFS). Employment follows ILO standards: persons who worked at least one hour for pay or profit during the reference week. Data are published annually and quarterly by Eurostat.
global_indicators.8-4-1-definition: The long-term unemployment rate is the proportion of people who have been unemployed for 12 months or more, expressed as a percentage of the active labour force. Long-term unemployment indicates a structural labour market problem associated with skills deterioration and social exclusion. Data are based on the EU Labour Force Survey.
global_indicators.8-4-1-intention: Long-term unemployment erodes skills, reduces employability and increases the risk of poverty and social exclusion. Addressing it requires active labour market policies, retraining programmes and social support. Progress means a sustained reduction in the long-term unemployment rate.
global_indicators.8-4-1-methodology: Data are collected through the EU Labour Force Survey (EU-LFS). Unemployment follows ILO standards: persons without a job, available for work and actively seeking employment. The long-term unemployed have been unemployed for 12 months or more. Data are published annually by Eurostat.
global_indicators.8-4-2-title: Domestic material consumption, domestic material consumption per capita, and domestic material consumption per GDP
global_indicators.8-5-1-definition: The NEET rate measures the proportion of young people aged 15 to 29 who are not in employment, education or training, expressed as a percentage of the total population in that age group. It identifies young people at risk of labour market exclusion and social marginalisation. Data are based on the EU Labour Force Survey.
global_indicators.8-5-1-intention: Young people who are NEET face long-term risks to their employment prospects, earnings and social integration. Reducing the NEET rate requires investment in education, vocational training and active labour market policies. Progress means a sustained reduction in the proportion of young people outside employment, education and training.
global_indicators.8-5-1-methodology: Data are collected through the EU Labour Force Survey (EU-LFS). NEET status combines information on employment status and participation in education or training in the four weeks preceding the survey. Data are published annually.
global_indicators.8-5-1-title: Young people neither in employment nor in education or training (NEET)
global_indicators.8-5-2-title: Unemployment rate, by sex, age and persons with disabilities
global_indicators.8-6-1-definition: This indicator measures the number of fatal accidents at work per 100,000 persons employed. A fatal accident at work is defined as an accident that leads to the death of the victim within one year of the accident. Data are collected through the European Statistics on Accidents at Work (ESAW).
global_indicators.8-6-1-intention: Ensuring safe and healthy working conditions is a fundamental dimension of decent work. Fatal accidents at work represent a preventable loss of life with severe consequences for workers, families and society. Progress means a sustained reduction in the rate of fatal accidents at work.
global_indicators.8-6-1-methodology: Data are compiled by Eurostat through the European Statistics on Accidents at Work (ESAW) methodology. The indicator covers all accidents at work that result in the death of the victim within one year. Data are published annually.
global_indicators.8-60-title: Fatal accidents at work per 100 000 workers
global_indicators.8-7-1-title: Proportion and number of children aged 5–17 years engaged in child labour, by sex and age
global_indicators.8-8-1-title: Fatal and non-fatal occupational injuries per 100,000 workers, by sex and migrant status
global_indicators.8-8-2-title: Level of national compliance with labour rights (freedom of association and collective bargaining) based on International Labour Organization (ILO) textual sources and national legislation, by sex and migrant status
global_indicators.8-9-1-title: Tourism direct GDP as a proportion of total GDP and in growth rate
global_indicators.8-9-2-title: Proportion of jobs in sustainable tourism industries out of total tourism jobs
global_indicators.8-a-1-title: Aid for Trade commitments and disbursements
global_indicators.8-b-1-title: Existence of a developed and operationalized national strategy for youth employment, as a distinct strategy or as part of a national employment strategy
global_indicators.9-1-1-definition: This indicator measures gross domestic expenditure on research and development (GERD) as a percentage of GDP. R&D expenditure covers all creative and systematic work to increase knowledge and devise new applications. It is a key indicator for monitoring innovation intensity. Data are compiled by Eurostat from national R&D surveys.
global_indicators.9-1-1-intention: Investment in R&D is a key driver of innovation, competitiveness and long-term productivity growth. Increasing R&D expenditure helps develop new technologies, improve processes and create high-quality jobs. Progress means a sustained increase in R&D expenditure as a share of GDP.
global_indicators.9-1-1-methodology: Data are collected through national R&D surveys following the OECD Frascati Manual. GERD covers all R&D performed on national territory regardless of funding source, including basic research, applied research and experimental development. Data are published annually by Eurostat.
global_indicators.9-1-1-title: Research and development expenditure as share of GDP
global_indicators.9-1-2-title: Passenger and freight volumes, by mode of transport
global_indicators.9-2-1-definition: This indicator measures the number of researchers in full-time equivalents (FTE) per million inhabitants. Researchers are professionals engaged in creating new knowledge, products, processes and systems. Data are compiled by Eurostat from national R&D statistics.
global_indicators.9-2-1-intention: Researchers are a key input to the innovation process. A larger research workforce drives scientific progress and economic competitiveness. Progress means an increasing number of researchers per million inhabitants across all sectors of the economy.
global_indicators.9-2-1-methodology: Data are compiled by Eurostat from R&D surveys following the OECD Frascati Manual. Researchers are counted in full-time equivalents to account for part-time work. Data cover business enterprise, government, higher education and private non-profit sectors.
global_indicators.9-2-1-title: Researchers in full-time equivalents per million inhabitants
global_indicators.9-2-2-title: Manufacturing employment as a proportion of total employment
global_indicators.9-3-1-definition: This indicator measures the number of patent applications filed with the European Patent Office (EPO) per million inhabitants. Patents protect inventions and indicate innovation output. A higher number reflects greater innovative activity. Data are compiled by Eurostat from EPO records.
global_indicators.9-3-1-intention: Patent applications are a widely used proxy for innovation output. Countries with strong patent activity benefit from technological progress and competitive advantage. Progress means a sustained increase in patent applications per million inhabitants.
global_indicators.9-3-1-methodology: Data are compiled by Eurostat from EPO records based on the residence of the inventor. Applications are counted at the priority date and attributed to the year of first filing. Data are published annually.
global_indicators.9-3-1-title: Patent applications to the European Patent Office
global_indicators.9-3-2-title: Proportion of small-scale industries with a loan or line of credit
global_indicators.9-4-1-definition: This indicator measures the share of high-technology products in total exports of manufactured goods, expressed as a percentage. High-technology products have high R&D intensity, such as aerospace, computers, pharmaceuticals and electronics. Data are compiled by Eurostat from trade statistics.
global_indicators.9-4-1-intention: A high share of high-tech exports reflects technological competitiveness and innovation capacity. Developing high-tech industries supports quality job creation and sustainable growth. Progress means an increasing share of high-technology products in total exports.
global_indicators.9-4-1-methodology: Data are compiled from trade statistics (COMEXT) using the OECD definition of high-technology sectors. High-technology products are classified using the Standard International Trade Classification (SITC). Data are published annually by Eurostat.
global_indicators.9-4-1-title: Share of high-tech exports in total exports
global_indicators.9-40-title: Patent applications to the European Patent Office
global_indicators.9-5-1-definition: This indicator measures the proportion of households with broadband internet access, expressed as a percentage of all households. Broadband includes fixed (DSL, cable, fibre) and mobile broadband connections. Data are collected through the EU Survey on ICT Usage in Households and by Individuals.
global_indicators.9-5-1-intention: Broadband access is essential for participation in the digital economy, access to public services and social inclusion. Expanding access, particularly in rural areas, is key to reducing the digital divide. Progress means an increasing proportion of households connected to broadband.
global_indicators.9-5-1-methodology: Data are collected through the EU ICT Survey, conducted annually. The indicator covers fixed and mobile broadband connections with download speeds of at least 144 Kbps. Data are published annually by Eurostat.
global_indicators.9-5-2-title: Researchers (in full-time equivalent) per million inhabitants
global_indicators.9-50-title: Share of busses and trains in inland passenger transport
global_indicators.9-6-1-definition: This indicator measures the share of rail and inland waterways in total inland freight transport, expressed as a percentage of total tonne-kilometres. It reflects the modal split of freight transport and the use of more sustainable modes. Data are compiled by Eurostat from national transport statistics.
global_indicators.9-6-1-intention: Shifting freight from road to rail and inland waterways reduces greenhouse gas emissions, congestion and accidents. Increasing the share of these sustainable modes is a key EU transport policy objective. Progress means an increasing share of rail and inland waterways in total inland freight transport.
global_indicators.9-6-1-methodology: Data are compiled by Eurostat from national transport statistics under EU transport data regulations. Freight transport is measured in tonne-kilometres. Rail and inland waterways are compared to total inland freight (road, rail and inland waterways combined). Data are published annually.
global_indicators.9-6-1-title: Share of rail and inland waterways in freight transport
global_indicators.9-60-title: Share of rail and inland waterways activity in inland freight transport
global_indicators.9-a-1-title: Total official international support (official development assistance plus other official flows) to infrastructure
global_indicators.9-b-1-title: Proportion of medium and high-tech industry value added in total value added
global_indicators.9-c-1-title: Proportion of population covered by a mobile network, by technology

global_targets.1-1-title: By 2030, eradicate extreme poverty for all people everywhere, currently measured as people living on less than $1.25 a day
global_targets.1-2-title: By 2030, reduce at least by half the proportion of men, women and children of all ages living in poverty in all its dimensions according to national definitions
global_targets.1-3-title: Implement nationally appropriate social protection systems and measures for all, including floors, and by 2030 achieve substantial coverage of the poor and the vulnerable
global_targets.1-4-title: By 2030, ensure that all men and women, in particular the poor and the vulnerable, have equal rights to economic resources, as well as access to basic services, ownership and control over land and other forms of property, inheritance, natural resources, appropriate new technology and financial services, including microfinance
global_targets.1-5-title: By 2030, build the resilience of the poor and those in vulnerable situations and reduce their exposure and vulnerability to climate-related extreme events and other economic, social and environmental shocks and disasters
global_targets.1-a-title: Ensure significant mobilization of resources from a variety of sources, including through enhanced development cooperation, in order to provide adequate and predictable means for developing countries, in particular least developed countries, to implement programmes and policies to end poverty in all its dimensions
global_targets.1-b-title: Create sound policy frameworks at the national, regional and international levels, based on pro-poor and gender-sensitive development strategies, to support accelerated investment in poverty eradication actions
global_targets.10-1-title: By 2030, progressively achieve and sustain income growth of the bottom 40 per cent of the population at a rate higher than the national average
global_targets.10-2-title: By 2030, empower and promote the social, economic and political inclusion of all, irrespective of age, sex, disability, race, ethnicity, origin, religion or economic or other status
global_targets.10-3-title: Ensure equal opportunity and reduce inequalities of outcome, including by eliminating discriminatory laws, policies and practices and promoting appropriate legislation, policies and action in this regard
global_targets.10-4-title: Adopt policies, especially fiscal, wage and social protection policies, and progressively achieve greater equality
global_targets.10-5-title: Improve the regulation and monitoring of global financial markets and institutions and strengthen the implementation of such regulations
global_targets.10-6-title: Ensure enhanced representation and voice for developing countries in decision-making in global international economic and financial institutions in order to deliver more effective, credible, accountable and legitimate institutions
global_targets.10-7-title: Facilitate orderly, safe, regular and responsible migration and mobility of people, including through the implementation of planned and well-managed migration policies
global_targets.10-a-title: Implement the principle of special and differential treatment for developing countries, in particular least developed countries, in accordance with World Trade Organization agreements
global_targets.10-b-title: Encourage official development assistance and financial flows, including foreign direct investment, to States where the need is greatest, in particular least developed countries, African countries, small island developing States and landlocked developing countries, in accordance with their national plans and programmes
global_targets.10-c-title: By 2030, reduce to less than 3 per cent the transaction costs of migrant remittances and eliminate remittance corridors with costs higher than 5 per cent
global_targets.11-1-title: By 2030, ensure access for all to adequate, safe and affordable housing and basic services and upgrade slums
global_targets.11-2-title: By 2030, provide access to safe, affordable, accessible and sustainable transport systems for all, improving road safety, notably by expanding public transport, with special attention to the needs of those in vulnerable situations, women, children, persons with disabilities and older persons
global_targets.11-3-title: By 2030, enhance inclusive and sustainable urbanization and capacity for participatory, integrated and sustainable human settlement planning and management in all countries
global_targets.11-4-title: Strengthen efforts to protect and safeguard the world’s cultural and natural heritage
global_targets.11-5-title: By 2030, significantly reduce the number of deaths and the number of people affected and substantially decrease the direct economic losses relative to global gross domestic product caused by disasters, including water-related disasters, with a focus on protecting the poor and people in vulnerable situations
global_targets.11-6-title: By 2030, reduce the adverse per capita environmental impact of cities, including by paying special attention to air quality and municipal and other waste management
global_targets.11-7-title: By 2030, provide universal access to safe, inclusive and accessible, green and public spaces, in particular for women and children, older persons and persons with disabilities
global_targets.11-a-title: Support positive economic, social and environmental links between urban, peri-urban and rural areas by strengthening national and regional development planning
global_targets.11-b-title: By 2020, substantially increase the number of cities and human settlements adopting and implementing integrated policies and plans towards inclusion, resource efficiency, mitigation and adaptation to climate change, resilience to disasters, and develop and implement, in line with the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030, holistic disaster risk management at all levels
global_targets.11-c-title: Support least developed countries, including through financial and technical assistance, in building sustainable and resilient buildings utilizing local materials
global_targets.12-1-title: Implement the 10‐Year Framework of Programmes on Sustainable Consumption and Production Patterns, all countries taking action, with developed countries taking the lead, taking into account the development and capabilities of developing countries
global_targets.12-2-title: By 2030, achieve the sustainable management and efficient use of natural resources
global_targets.12-3-title: By 2030, halve per capita global food waste at the retail and consumer levels and reduce food losses along production and supply chains, including post-harvest losses
global_targets.12-4-title: By 2020, achieve the environmentally sound management of chemicals and all wastes throughout their life cycle, in accordance with agreed international frameworks, and significantly reduce their release to air, water and soil in order to minimize their adverse impacts on human health and the environment
global_targets.12-5-title: By 2030, substantially reduce waste generation through prevention, reduction, recycling and reuse
global_targets.12-6-title: Encourage companies, especially large and transnational companies, to adopt sustainable practices and to integrate sustainability information into their reporting cycle
global_targets.12-7-title: Promote public procurement practices that are sustainable, in accordance with national policies and priorities
global_targets.12-8-title: By 2030, ensure that people everywhere have the relevant information and awareness for sustainable development and lifestyles in harmony with nature
global_targets.12-a-title: Support developing countries to strengthen their scientific and technological capacity to move towards more sustainable patterns of consumption and production
global_targets.12-b-title: Develop and implement tools to monitor sustainable development impacts for sustainable tourism that creates jobs and promotes local culture and products
global_targets.12-c-title: Rationalize inefficient fossil-fuel subsidies that encourage wasteful consumption by removing market distortions, in accordance with national circumstances, including by restructuring taxation and phasing out those harmful subsidies, where they exist, to reflect their environmental impacts, taking fully into account the specific needs and conditions of developing countries and minimizing the possible adverse impacts on their development in a manner that protects the poor and the affected communities
global_targets.13-1-title: Strengthen resilience and adaptive capacity to climate-related hazards and natural disasters in all countries
global_targets.13-2-title: Integrate climate change measures into national policies, strategies and planning
global_targets.13-3-title: Improve education, awareness-raising and human and institutional capacity on climate change mitigation, adaptation, impact reduction and early warning
global_targets.13-a-title: Implement the commitment undertaken by developed-country parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change to a goal of mobilizing jointly $100 billion annually by 2020 from all sources to address the needs of developing countries in the context of meaningful mitigation actions and transparency on implementation and fully operationalize the Green Climate Fund through its capitalization as soon as possible
global_targets.13-b-title: Promote mechanisms for raising capacity for effective climate change-related planning and management in least developed countries and small island developing States, including focusing on women, youth and local and marginalized communities
global_targets.14-1-title: By 2025, prevent and significantly reduce marine pollution of all kinds, in particular from land-based activities, including marine debris and nutrient pollution
global_targets.14-2-title: By 2020, sustainably manage and protect marine and coastal ecosystems to avoid significant adverse impacts, including by strengthening their resilience, and take action for their restoration in order to achieve healthy and productive oceans
global_targets.14-3-title: Minimize and address the impacts of ocean acidification, including through enhanced scientific cooperation at all levels
global_targets.14-4-title: By 2020, effectively regulate harvesting and end overfishing, illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing and destructive fishing practices and implement science-based management plans, in order to restore fish stocks in the shortest time feasible, at least to levels that can produce maximum sustainable yield as determined by their biological characteristics
global_targets.14-5-title: By 2020, conserve at least 10 per cent of coastal and marine areas, consistent with national and international law and based on the best available scientific information
global_targets.14-6-title: By 2020, prohibit certain forms of fisheries subsidies which contribute to overcapacity and overfishing, eliminate subsidies that contribute to illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing and refrain from introducing new such subsidies, recognizing that appropriate and effective special and differential treatment for developing and least developed countries should be an integral part of the World Trade Organization fisheries subsidies negotiation
global_targets.14-7-title: By 2030, increase the economic benefits to small island developing States and least developed countries from the sustainable use of marine resources, including through sustainable management of fisheries, aquaculture and tourism
global_targets.14-a-title: Increase scientific knowledge, develop research capacity and transfer marine technology, taking into account the Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission Criteria and Guidelines on the Transfer of Marine Technology, in order to improve ocean health and to enhance the contribution of marine biodiversity to the development of developing countries, in particular small island developing States and least developed countries
global_targets.14-b-title: Provide access for small-scale artisanal fishers to marine resources and markets
global_targets.14-c-title: Enhance the conservation and sustainable use of oceans and their resources by implementing international law as reflected in the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, which provides the legal framework for the conservation and sustainable use of oceans and their resources, as recalled in paragraph 158 of “The future we want”
global_targets.15-1-title: By 2020, ensure the conservation, restoration and sustainable use of terrestrial and inland freshwater ecosystems and their services, in particular forests, wetlands, mountains and drylands, in line with obligations under international agreements
global_targets.15-2-title: By 2020, promote the implementation of sustainable management of all types of forests, halt deforestation, restore degraded forests and substantially increase afforestation and reforestation globally
global_targets.15-3-title: By 2030, combat desertification, restore degraded land and soil, including land affected by desertification, drought and floods, and strive to achieve a land degradation-neutral world
global_targets.15-4-title: By 2030, ensure the conservation of mountain ecosystems, including their biodiversity, in order to enhance their capacity to provide benefits that are essential for sustainable development
global_targets.15-5-title: Take urgent and significant action to reduce the degradation of natural habitats, halt the loss of biodiversity and, by 2020, protect and prevent the extinction of threatened species
global_targets.15-6-title: Promote fair and equitable sharing of the benefits arising from the utilization of genetic resources and promote appropriate access to such resources, as internationally agreed
global_targets.15-7-title: Take urgent action to end poaching and trafficking of protected species of flora and fauna and address both demand and supply of illegal wildlife products
global_targets.15-8-title: By 2020, introduce measures to prevent the introduction and significantly reduce the impact of invasive alien species on land and water ecosystems and control or eradicate the priority species
global_targets.15-9-title: By 2020, integrate ecosystem and biodiversity values into national and local planning, development processes, poverty reduction strategies and accounts
global_targets.15-a-title: Mobilize and significantly increase financial resources from all sources to conserve and sustainably use biodiversity and ecosystems
global_targets.15-b-title: Mobilize significant resources from all sources and at all levels to finance sustainable forest management and provide adequate incentives to developing countries to advance such management, including for conservation and reforestation
global_targets.15-c-title: Enhance global support for efforts to combat poaching and trafficking of protected species, including by increasing the capacity of local communities to pursue sustainable livelihood opportunities
global_targets.16-1-title: Significantly reduce all forms of violence and related death rates everywhere
global_targets.16-10-title: Ensure public access to information and protect fundamental freedoms, in accordance with national legislation and international agreements
global_targets.16-2-title: End abuse, exploitation, trafficking and all forms of violence against and torture of children
global_targets.16-3-title: Promote the rule of law at the national and international levels and ensure equal access to justice for all
global_targets.16-4-title: By 2030, significantly reduce illicit financial and arms flows, strengthen the recovery and return of stolen assets and combat all forms of organized crime
global_targets.16-5-title: Substantially reduce corruption and bribery in all their forms
global_targets.16-6-title: Develop effective, accountable and transparent institutions at all levels
global_targets.16-7-title: Ensure responsive, inclusive, participatory and representative decision-making at all levels
global_targets.16-8-title: Broaden and strengthen the participation of developing countries in the institutions of global governance
global_targets.16-9-title: By 2030, provide legal identity for all, including birth registration
global_targets.16-a-title: Strengthen relevant national institutions, including through international cooperation, for building capacity at all levels, in particular in developing countries, to prevent violence and combat terrorism and crime
global_targets.16-b-title: Promote and enforce non-discriminatory laws and policies for sustainable development
global_targets.17-1-title: Strengthen domestic resource mobilization, including through international support to developing countries, to improve domestic capacity for tax and other revenue collection
global_targets.17-10-title: Promote a universal, rules-based, open, non‐discriminatory and equitable multilateral trading system under the World Trade Organization, including through the conclusion of negotiations under its Doha Development Agenda
global_targets.17-11-title: Significantly increase the exports of developing countries, in particular with a view to doubling the least developed countries’ share of global exports by 2020
global_targets.17-12-title: Realize timely implementation of duty-free and quota-free market access on a lasting basis for all least developed countries, consistent with World Trade Organization decisions, including by ensuring that preferential rules of origin applicable to imports from least developed countries are transparent and simple, and contribute to facilitating market access
global_targets.17-13-title: Enhance global macroeconomic stability, including through policy coordination and policy coherence
global_targets.17-14-title: Enhance policy coherence for sustainable development
global_targets.17-15-title: Respect each country’s policy space and leadership to establish and implement policies for poverty eradication and sustainable development
global_targets.17-16-title: Enhance the Global Partnership for Sustainable Development, complemented by multi-stakeholder partnerships that mobilize and share knowledge, expertise, technology and financial resources, to support the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals in all countries, in particular developing countries
global_targets.17-17-title: Encourage and promote effective public, public-private and civil society partnerships, building on the experience and resourcing strategies of partnerships
global_targets.17-18-title: By 2020, enhance capacity-building support to developing countries, including for least developed countries and small island developing States, to increase significantly the availability of high-quality, timely and reliable data disaggregated by income, gender, age, race, ethnicity, migratory status, disability, geographic location and other characteristics relevant in national contexts
global_targets.17-19-title: By 2030, build on existing initiatives to develop measurements of progress on sustainable development that complement gross domestic product, and support statistical capacity-building in developing countries
global_targets.17-2-title: Developed countries to implement fully their official development assistance commitments, including the commitment by many developed countries to achieve the target of 0.7 per cent of gross national income for official development assistance (ODA/GNI) to developing countries and 0.15 to 0.20 per cent of ODA/GNI to least developed countries; ODA providers are encouraged to consider setting a target to provide at least 0.20 per cent of ODA/GNI to least developed countries
global_targets.17-3-title: Mobilize additional financial resources for developing countries from multiple sources
global_targets.17-4-title: Assist developing countries in attaining long-term debt sustainability through coordinated policies aimed at fostering debt financing, debt relief and debt restructuring, as appropriate, and address the external debt of highly indebted poor countries to reduce debt distress
global_targets.17-5-title: Adopt and implement investment promotion regimes for least developed countries
global_targets.17-6-title: Enhance North-South, South-South and triangular regional and international cooperation on and access to science, technology and innovation and enhance knowledge-sharing on mutually agreed terms, including through improved coordination among existing mechanisms, in particular at the United Nations level, and through a global technology facilitation mechanism
global_targets.17-7-title: Promote the development, transfer, dissemination and diffusion of environmentally sound technologies to developing countries on favourable terms, including on concessional and preferential terms, as mutually agreed
global_targets.17-8-title: Fully operationalize the technology bank and science, technology and innovation capacity-building mechanism for least developed countries by 2017 and enhance the use of enabling technology, in particular information and communications technology
global_targets.17-9-title: Enhance international support for implementing effective and targeted capacity-building in developing countries to support national plans to implement all the Sustainable Development Goals, including through North-South, South-South and triangular cooperation
global_targets.2-1-title: By 2030, end hunger and ensure access by all people, in particular the poor and people in vulnerable situations, including infants, to safe, nutritious and sufficient food all year round
global_targets.2-2-title: By 2030, end all forms of malnutrition, including achieving, by 2025, the internationally agreed targets on stunting and wasting in children under 5 years of age, and address the nutritional needs of adolescent girls, pregnant and lactating women and older persons
global_targets.2-3-title: By 2030, double the agricultural productivity and incomes of small-scale food producers, in particular women, indigenous peoples, family farmers, pastoralists and fishers, including through secure and equal access to land, other productive resources and inputs, knowledge, financial services, markets and opportunities for value addition and non-farm employment
global_targets.2-4-title: By 2030, ensure sustainable food production systems and implement resilient agricultural practices that increase productivity and production, that help maintain ecosystems, that strengthen capacity for adaptation to climate change, extreme weather, drought, flooding and other disasters and that progressively improve land and soil quality
global_targets.2-5-title: By 2020, maintain the genetic diversity of seeds, cultivated plants and farmed and domesticated animals and their related wild species, including through soundly managed and diversified seed and plant banks at the national, regional and international levels, and promote access to and fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from the utilization of genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge, as internationally agreed
global_targets.2-a-title: Increase investment, including through enhanced international cooperation, in rural infrastructure, agricultural research and extension services, technology development and plant and livestock gene banks in order to enhance agricultural productive capacity in developing countries, in particular least developed countries
global_targets.2-b-title: Correct and prevent trade restrictions and distortions in world agricultural markets, including through the parallel elimination of all forms of agricultural export subsidies and all export measures with equivalent effect, in accordance with the mandate of the Doha Development Round
global_targets.2-c-title: Adopt measures to ensure the proper functioning of food commodity markets and their derivatives and facilitate timely access to market information, including on food reserves, in order to help limit extreme food price volatility
global_targets.3-1-title: By 2030, reduce the global maternal mortality ratio to less than 70 per 100,000 live births
global_targets.3-2-title: By 2030, end preventable deaths of newborns and children under 5 years of age, with all countries aiming to reduce neonatal mortality to at least as low as 12 per 1,000 live births and under‐5 mortality to at least as low as 25 per 1,000 live births
global_targets.3-3-title: By 2030, end the epidemics of AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria and neglected tropical diseases and combat hepatitis, water-borne diseases and other communicable diseases
global_targets.3-4-title: By 2030, reduce by one third premature mortality from non-communicable diseases through prevention and treatment and promote mental health and well-being
global_targets.3-5-title: Strengthen the prevention and treatment of substance abuse, including narcotic drug abuse and harmful use of alcohol
global_targets.3-6-title: By 2020, halve the number of global deaths and injuries from road traffic accidents
global_targets.3-7-title: By 2030, ensure universal access to sexual and reproductive health-care services, including for family planning, information and education, and the integration of reproductive health into national strategies and programmes
global_targets.3-8-title: Achieve universal health coverage, including financial risk protection, access to quality essential health-care services and access to safe, effective, quality and affordable essential medicines and vaccines for all
global_targets.3-9-title: By 2030, substantially reduce the number of deaths and illnesses from hazardous chemicals and air, water and soil pollution and contamination
global_targets.3-a-title: Strengthen the implementation of the World Health Organization Framework Convention on Tobacco Control in all countries, as appropriate
global_targets.3-b-title: Support the research and development of vaccines and medicines for the communicable and non‐communicable diseases that primarily affect developing countries, provide access to affordable essential medicines and vaccines, in accordance with the Doha Declaration on the TRIPS Agreement and Public Health, which affirms the right of developing countries to use to the full the provisions in the Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights regarding flexibilities to protect public health, and, in particular, provide access to medicines for all
global_targets.3-c-title: Substantially increase health financing and the recruitment, development, training and retention of the health workforce in developing countries, especially in least developed countries and small island developing States
global_targets.3-d-title: Strengthen the capacity of all countries, in particular developing countries, for early warning, risk reduction and management of national and global health risks
global_targets.4-1-title: By 2030, ensure that all girls and boys complete free, equitable and quality primary and secondary education leading to relevant and effective learning outcomes
global_targets.4-2-title: By 2030, ensure that all girls and boys have access to quality early childhood development, care and pre‐primary education so that they are ready for primary education
global_targets.4-3-title: By 2030, ensure equal access for all women and men to affordable and quality technical, vocational and tertiary education, including university
global_targets.4-4-title: By 2030, substantially increase the number of youth and adults who have relevant skills, including technical and vocational skills, for employment, decent jobs and entrepreneurship
global_targets.4-5-title: By 2030, eliminate gender disparities in education and ensure equal access to all levels of education and vocational training for the vulnerable, including persons with disabilities, indigenous peoples and children in vulnerable situations
global_targets.4-6-title: By 2030, ensure that all youth and a substantial proportion of adults, both men and women, achieve literacy and numeracy
global_targets.4-7-title: By 2030, ensure that all learners acquire the knowledge and skills needed to promote sustainable development, including, among others, through education for sustainable development and sustainable lifestyles, human rights, gender equality, promotion of a culture of peace and non-violence, global citizenship and appreciation of cultural diversity and of culture’s contribution to sustainable development
global_targets.4-a-title: Build and upgrade education facilities that are child, disability and gender sensitive and provide safe, non-violent, inclusive and effective learning environments for all
global_targets.4-b-title: By 2020, substantially expand globally the number of scholarships available to developing countries, in particular least developed countries, small island developing States and African countries, for enrolment in higher education, including vocational training and information and communications technology, technical, engineering and scientific programmes, in developed countries and other developing countries
global_targets.4-c-title: By 2030, substantially increase the supply of qualified teachers, including through international cooperation for teacher training in developing countries, especially least developed countries and small island developing States
global_targets.5-1-title: End all forms of discrimination against all women and girls everywhere
global_targets.5-2-title: Eliminate all forms of violence against all women and girls in the public and private spheres, including trafficking and sexual and other types of exploitation
global_targets.5-3-title: Eliminate all harmful practices, such as child, early and forced marriage and female genital mutilation
global_targets.5-4-title: Recognize and value unpaid care and domestic work through the provision of public services, infrastructure and social protection policies and the promotion of shared responsibility within the household and the family as nationally appropriate
global_targets.5-5-title: Ensure women’s full and effective participation and equal opportunities for leadership at all levels of decision-making in political, economic and public life
global_targets.5-6-title: Ensure universal access to sexual and reproductive health and reproductive rights as agreed in accordance with the Programme of Action of the International Conference on Population and Development and the Beijing Platform for Action and the outcome documents of their review conferences
global_targets.5-a-title: Undertake reforms to give women equal rights to economic resources, as well as access to ownership and control over land and other forms of property, financial services, inheritance and natural resources, in accordance with national laws
global_targets.5-b-title: Enhance the use of enabling technology, in particular information and communications technology, to promote the empowerment of women
global_targets.5-c-title: Adopt and strengthen sound policies and enforceable legislation for the promotion of gender equality and the empowerment of all women and girls at all levels
global_targets.6-1-title: By 2030, achieve universal and equitable access to safe and affordable drinking water for all
global_targets.6-2-title: By 2030, achieve access to adequate and equitable sanitation and hygiene for all and end open defecation, paying special attention to the needs of women and girls and those in vulnerable situations
global_targets.6-3-title: By 2030, improve water quality by reducing pollution, eliminating dumping and minimizing release of hazardous chemicals and materials, halving the proportion of untreated wastewater and substantially increasing recycling and safe reuse globally
global_targets.6-4-title: By 2030, substantially increase water-use efficiency across all sectors and ensure sustainable withdrawals and supply of freshwater to address water scarcity and substantially reduce the number of people suffering from water scarcity
global_targets.6-5-title: By 2030, implement integrated water resources management at all levels, including through transboundary cooperation as appropriate
global_targets.6-6-title: By 2020, protect and restore water-related ecosystems, including mountains, forests, wetlands, rivers, aquifers and lakes
global_targets.6-a-title: By 2030, expand international cooperation and capacity-building support to developing countries in water- and sanitation-related activities and programmes, including water harvesting, desalination, water efficiency, wastewater treatment, recycling and reuse technologies
global_targets.6-b-title: Support and strengthen the participation of local communities in improving water and sanitation management
global_targets.7-1-title: By 2030, ensure universal access to affordable, reliable and modern energy services
global_targets.7-2-title: By 2030, increase substantially the share of renewable energy in the global energy mix
global_targets.7-3-title: By 2030, double the global rate of improvement in energy efficiency
global_targets.7-a-title: By 2030, enhance international cooperation to facilitate access to clean energy research and technology, including renewable energy, energy efficiency and advanced and cleaner fossil-fuel technology, and promote investment in energy infrastructure and clean energy technology
global_targets.7-b-title: By 2030, expand infrastructure and upgrade technology for supplying modern and sustainable energy services for all in developing countries, in particular least developed countries, small island developing States and landlocked developing countries, in accordance with their respective programmes of support
global_targets.8-1-title: Sustain per capita economic growth in accordance with national circumstances and, in particular, at least 7 per cent gross domestic product growth per annum in the least developed countries
global_targets.8-10-title: Strengthen the capacity of domestic financial institutions to encourage and expand access to banking, insurance and financial services for all
global_targets.8-2-title: Achieve higher levels of economic productivity through diversification, technological upgrading and innovation, including through a focus on high-value added and labour-intensive sectors
global_targets.8-3-title: Promote development-oriented policies that support productive activities, decent job creation, entrepreneurship, creativity and innovation, and encourage the formalization and growth of micro-, small- and medium-sized enterprises, including through access to financial services
global_targets.8-4-title: Improve progressively, through 2030, global resource efficiency in consumption and production and endeavour to decouple economic growth from environmental degradation, in accordance with the 10‐Year Framework of Programmes on Sustainable Consumption and Production, with developed countries taking the lead
global_targets.8-5-title: By 2030, achieve full and productive employment and decent work for all women and men, including for young people and persons with disabilities, and equal pay for work of equal value
global_targets.8-6-title: By 2020, substantially reduce the proportion of youth not in employment, education or training
global_targets.8-7-title: Take immediate and effective measures to eradicate forced labour, end modern slavery and human trafficking and secure the prohibition and elimination of the worst forms of child labour, including recruitment and use of child soldiers, and by 2025 end child labour in all its forms
global_targets.8-8-title: Protect labour rights and promote safe and secure working environments for all workers, including migrant workers, in particular women migrants, and those in precarious employment
global_targets.8-9-title: By 2030, devise and implement policies to promote sustainable tourism that creates jobs and promotes local culture and products
global_targets.8-a-title: Increase Aid for Trade support for developing countries, in particular least developed countries, including through the Enhanced Integrated Framework for Trade-related Technical Assistance to Least Developed Countries
global_targets.8-b-title: By 2020, develop and operationalize a global strategy for youth employment and implement the Global Jobs Pact of the International Labour Organization
global_targets.9-1-title: Develop quality, reliable, sustainable and resilient infrastructure, including regional and transborder infrastructure, to support economic development and human well-being, with a focus on affordable and equitable access for all
